title.zh: 卷七十五 列傳第六十三: 趙煚 趙芬 王韶 元巖 宇文㢸 伊婁謙 李圓通 郭榮 龐晃 李安 楊尚希 張煚 蘇孝慈 元壽
title.en: Volume 75 Biographies 63: Zhao Jiong, Zhao Fen, Wang Shao, Yuan Yan, Yu Wenbi, Yi Louqian, Li Yuantong, Guo Rong, Pang Huang, Li An, Yang Shangxi, Zhang Jiong, Su Xiaoci, Yuan Shou

translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jiong, Zhao Fen, Wang Shao, Yuan Yan, Yu Wenbi, Yi Louqian, Li Yuantong, Guo Rong, Pang Huang, Li An, Yang Shangxi, Zhang Jiong, Su Xiaoci, and Yuan Shou

sentences.zh: 趙煚 趙芬 王韶 元巖 宇文㢸 伊婁謙 李圓通 郭榮 龐晃 李安 楊尚希 張煚 蘇孝慈 元壽

translations.literal: Zhao Jiong, Zhao Fen, Wang Shao, Yuan Yan, Yu Wenbi, Yi Louqian, Li Yuantong, Guo Rong, Pang Huang, Li An, Yang Shangxi, Zhang Jiong, Su Xiaoci, Yuan Shou
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jiong, Zhao Fen, Wang Shao, Yuan Yan, Yu Wenbi, Yi Louqian, Li Yuantong, Guo Rong, Pang Huang, Li An, Yang Shangxi, Zhang Jiong, Su Xiaoci, and Yuan Shou

sentences.zh: 趙煚，字通賢，天水西人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Jiong, styled Tongxian, was a man of Xi in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jiong, whose courtesy name was Tongxian, came from Xi in Tianshui commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖超宗，魏河東太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chaozong was Administrator of Hedong in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chaozong had served as Administrator of Hedong under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 父仲懿，尚書左丞。

translations.literal: His father Zhongyi was Left Assistant in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongyi had been Left Assistant Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 煚少孤，養母至孝。

translations.literal: Jiong was orphaned young and nursed his mother with utmost filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong lost his father while still young and supported his mother with exemplary filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 年十四，有人盜伐其父墓中樹者，煚對之號慟，因執送官。

translations.literal: At fourteen, when someone stole and cut trees from his father's tomb, Jiong wailed before him and had him seized and sent to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: When he was fourteen, he found a man stealing timber from his father's grave; Jiong wept aloud in grief before him, then seized the man and handed him over to the magistrates.

sentences.zh: 見魏右僕射周惠達，長揖不拜，自述孤苦，涕淚交集，惠達為之隕涕歎息者久之。

translations.literal: When he met Zhou Huida, Right Vice Director of the Wei, he made a long bow without prostrating, described his orphaned hardship, and tears mingled; Huida shed tears and sighed over him for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: On meeting Zhou Huida, the Wei dynasty's Right Vice Director, he gave a deep bow but did not prostrate himself, then told of his orphaned plight until tears streamed down his face; Huida wept and sighed over him for a long time.

sentences.zh: 及長，沈深有器局，略涉書記。

translations.literal: When grown, he was deep and steady with capacity and vision, and had some acquaintance with documents.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he was grave and far-sighted, possessed of real capacity, and had some training in written administration.

sentences.zh: 周文帝引為相府參軍事。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou summoned him as Staff Officer in the Chancellor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou brought him into service as a staff officer in the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 從破洛陽。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the campaign that captured Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及班師，煚請留撫納亡叛，從之。

translations.literal: When the army withdrew, Jiong asked to remain to pacify and receive deserters and rebels, and this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: When the army withdrew, Jiong asked permission to stay behind to pacify the region and win over deserters and rebels; his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 煚於是帥所領與齊人前後五戰，斬獲甚眾，以功封平定縣男。

translations.literal: Jiong then led his command in five battles with the Qi, before and after, beheading and capturing many; for merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingding county.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong then led his troops through five engagements with the Qi, killing and capturing a great number of the enemy; for this service he was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingding.

sentences.zh: 累轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Director in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 周閔帝受禪，遷硤州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min of Zhou received the abdication, Jiong was moved to be Governor of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min of Zhou ascended the throne, Jiong was appointed Governor of Xia province.

sentences.zh: 蠻酋向天王以兵攻信陵、秭歸，煚襲擊破之，二郡獲全。

translations.literal: The barbarian chieftain Xiang Tianwang attacked Xinling and Zigui with troops; Jiong struck in a surprise attack and defeated him, and the two commanderies were preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal chieftain Xiang Tianwang attacked Xinling and Zigui with an army; Jiong caught him in a surprise attack and routed him, saving both commanderies.

sentences.zh: 時周人於江南岸置安蜀城以禦陳，屬霖雨數旬，城頹者百餘步。

translations.literal: At that time the Zhou had set up Ancheng on the south bank of the Yangzi to guard against Chen; it happened that rain fell for many tens of days, and more than a hundred paces of the wall collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou had built Ancheng on the south bank of the Yangzi to hold the Chen at bay; after weeks of steady rain, more than a hundred paces of the wall had collapsed.

sentences.zh: 蠻酋鄭南鄉叛，引陳將吳明徹欲掩安蜀。

translations.literal: The barbarian chieftain Zheng Nanxiang rebelled and brought in the Chen general Wu Mingche, intending to take Ancheng by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal leader Zheng Nanxiang rebelled and enlisted the Chen general Wu Mingche in a plan to seize Ancheng by surprise.

sentences.zh: 議者皆勸煚益修守禦，煚不從，乃遣使說誘江外生蠻向武陽，令乘虛掩襲南鄉所居，獲其父母妻子。

translations.literal: Those in council all urged Jiong to strengthen defenses further; Jiong did not follow them, but instead sent envoys to persuade and entice the raw barbarians beyond the river, Xiang Wuyang, to strike by surprise at Nanxiang's dwelling while he was exposed, and seized his parents, wife, and children.
translations.idiomatic: Counselors all urged Jiong to strengthen the fortifications, but he refused; instead he sent envoys to win over Xiang Wuyang, a tribal leader beyond the river, and had him raid Nanxiang's stronghold while it was undefended, capturing his parents, wife, and children.

sentences.zh: 南鄉聞之，其黨各散，陳兵亦遁。

translations.literal: When Nanxiang heard of it, his partisans each scattered, and the Chen troops also fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanxiang heard what had happened, his followers scattered, and the Chen army withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 明年，吳明徹屢為寇患，煚與前後十六戰，每挫其鋒。

translations.literal: The next year Wu Mingche repeatedly raided as a scourge; Jiong fought him in sixteen battles before and after, each time blunting his edge.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wu Mingche raided repeatedly; Jiong met him in sixteen engagements and each time drove back his advance.

sentences.zh: 以功授開府儀同三司，再遷戶部中大夫。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted Grand Master with Honored Title Equal to the Three Dukes, and was promoted again to Grand Master in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: For these achievements he was made Grand Master with the Honored Title Equal to the Three Dukes, and was soon promoted again to Grand Master in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 周武帝欲收齊河南地，煚諫曰：「河南洛陽，四面受敵，縱得不可以守。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou wished to recover the Henan lands of Qi; Jiong remonstrated, saying, "Henan and Luoyang are attacked on all four sides; even if taken they cannot be held.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou planned to recover Qi's Henan territories, Jiong advised him: "Luoyang in Henan is exposed on every side; even if we take it, we cannot hold it.

sentences.zh: 請從河北直指太原，傾其巢穴，可一舉以定。」

translations.literal: I ask that from Hebei we strike straight at Taiyuan and overturn their nest; in one move it can be settled."
translations.idiomatic: Strike north from Hebei straight at Taiyuan and destroy their base at a stroke—that is how the matter can be settled in one campaign."

sentences.zh: 帝不納，師竟無功。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not accept this; the army in the end achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed him, and the campaign ended in failure.

sentences.zh: 尋從上柱國於翼自三鴉道伐陳，克十九城而還。

translations.literal: Soon after he followed the Grand Pillar of State Yu Yi in attacking Chen by the Sanya route, captured nineteen cities, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed the Grand Pillar of State Yu Yi on an expedition against Chen by the Sanya route, took nineteen cities, and returned.

sentences.zh: 以讒毀，功不見錄。

translations.literal: Because of slander and defamation, his achievements were not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Slanderers maligned him, and his achievements went unrecognized.

sentences.zh: 累遷禦正上大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Master of the Imperial Rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Grand Master of Imperial Rectitude.

sentences.zh: 煚與宗伯斛斯徵素不協，徵後出為齊州刺史，坐事下獄，自知罪重，遂逾獄走。

translations.literal: Jiong and the Minister of Rites Husu Zheng had long been at odds; Zheng was later sent out as Governor of Qi and, implicated in an offense, was thrown into prison; knowing his crime was grave, he escaped over the prison wall and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong and Husu Zheng, the Minister of Rites, had never been on good terms. Zheng was later posted as Governor of Qi, then imprisoned for an offense; knowing his crime was capital, he broke out of prison and fled.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，購之甚急。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged and offered a reward for him with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and put a high price on his head.

sentences.zh: 煚密奏曰：「徵自以罪重，懼死遁逃，若不北走匈奴，則南奔吳越。

translations.literal: Jiong secretly memorialized, saying, "Zheng, knowing his crime is grave, fears death and has fled; if he does not flee north to the Xiongnu, he will flee south to Wu and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong submitted a secret memorial: "Zheng knows his crime is grave and has fled for fear of execution; if he does not go north to the Xiongnu, he will go south to Wu and Yue.

sentences.zh: 徵雖愚陋，久曆清顯，奔彼敵國，無益聖朝。

translations.literal: Though Zheng is foolish and lowly, he has long held clear and eminent office; if he flees to those enemy states, it will not benefit the holy court.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zheng is a man of little talent, he has long held high office; flight to an enemy state would do the dynasty no good.

sentences.zh: 今炎旱為災，可因茲大赦。」

translations.literal: Now scorching drought is a disaster; we may take this occasion for a great amnesty."
translations.idiomatic: The land is stricken with drought and heat; let Your Majesty use this occasion to proclaim a general amnesty."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 徵賴而免，煚卒不言。

translations.literal: Zheng relied on this and was spared; Jiong to the end did not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was spared by the amnesty, and Jiong never spoke of what he had done.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，加上開府，再遷大宗伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was Chancellor, Jiong was given the additional title of Grand Master Opening the Office, and was promoted again to Grand Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was still chancellor, Jiong was made Grand Master Opening the Office and was soon promoted again to Grand Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，煚授璽紱。

translations.literal: When the throne was taken, Jiong presented the seal and cord.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, it was Jiong who presented the imperial seal and cord.

sentences.zh: 進位大將軍，賜爵金城郡公，拜相州刺史。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand General, granted the title Duke of Jincheng commandery, and appointed Governor of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand General, ennobled as Duke of Jincheng commandery, and appointed Governor of Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以煚習故事，徵拜尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: The court, because Jiong was versed in precedent, summoned and appointed him Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jiong was expert in court precedent, the court recalled him and appointed him Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以忤旨出為陝州刺史，轉冀州刺史，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: Before long, for going against the imperial will he was sent out as Governor of Shan, then transferred to Governor of Ji, where he had great authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he offended the emperor and was sent out as Governor of Shan, then transferred to Ji, where he ruled with a formidable blend of sternness and benevolence.

sentences.zh: 煚嘗有疾，百姓賓士，爭為祈禱，其得人情如此。

translations.literal: When Jiong once fell ill, commoners and guests alike vied to pray for him; such was the measure in which he won people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Jiong fell ill, townspeople and visitors alike crowded in to pray for his recovery—such was the affection he commanded.

sentences.zh: 冀州市多奸詐，煚為銅鬥鐵尺。

translations.literal: In the markets of Ji there was much fraud; Jiong made bronze bushels and iron rulers.
translations.idiomatic: The markets of Ji were rife with short measure and fraud; Jiong had standard bronze bushels and iron rulers made.

sentences.zh: 置於肆，百姓便之。

translations.literal: He placed them in the markets, and the people found them convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He placed them in the marketplaces, to the great convenience of the people.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而嘉焉，頒之天下，以為常法。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and commended this, promulgated it throughout the realm, and made it standing law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of it with approval and ordered the practice adopted empire-wide as permanent law.

sentences.zh: 嘗有人盜煚田中蒿，為吏所執。

translations.literal: Once someone stole mugwort from Jiong's fields and was seized by clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Once a man was caught by the clerks stealing mugwort from Jiong's fields.

sentences.zh: 煚曰：「此乃刺史不能宣風化，彼何罪也？」

translations.literal: Jiong said, "This is because the governor cannot spread transforming influence; what crime is his?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiong said, "This only shows that I as governor have failed to teach the people properly—what crime has he committed?"

sentences.zh: 慰諭遣之，令人載蒿一車賜盜者，盜愧過於重刑。

translations.literal: He comforted and instructed him and sent him away, then had a cartload of mugwort given to the thief; the thief's shame exceeded any heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He comforted the man and sent him home, then had a full cartload of mugwort delivered to him as a gift; the thief was more ashamed than if he had suffered the harshest penalty.

sentences.zh: 帝幸洛陽，煚來朝，帝勞之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor visited Luoyang, Jiong came to audience and the Emperor comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Luoyang, Jiong came to court and was received with words of praise and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子義臣嗣，位至太子洗馬。

translations.literal: His son Yichen succeeded him and rose to Groom of the Heir Apparent's Stud.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yichen succeeded him and rose to the post of Groom in the Heir Apparent's Stud.

sentences.zh: 後同楊諒反，誅。

translations.literal: Later he joined Yang Liang's rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Yang Liang's rebellion and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 趙芬，字士茂，天水西人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Fen, styled Shimao, was a man of Xi in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fen, whose courtesy name was Shimao, came from Xi in Tianshui commandery.

sentences.zh: 父諒，周秦州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Liang was Governor of Qin in Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liang had been Governor of Qin under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 芬少有辯智，頗涉經史。

translations.literal: Fen in youth had eloquence and wisdom and had dipped considerably into the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Fen was quick-witted and articulate and had read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 周引為相府鎧曹參軍。

translations.literal: Zhou summoned him as Staff Officer in the Armor Bureau of the Chancellor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou court brought him in as a staff officer in the armor bureau of the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 曆記室，累遷開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He passed through the Record Office and was promoted in succession to Grand Master with Honored Title Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the secretariat and rose in succession to Grand Master with the Honored Title Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 性強濟，所居之職，皆有聲績。

translations.literal: By nature he was forceful and resourceful; in every post he held there was reputation and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Forceful and resourceful by nature, he left a record of distinction in every post he held.

sentences.zh: 周武帝親總萬機，拜內史下大夫，轉小禦正。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou personally took charge of all affairs, Fen was appointed Grand Master in the Inner Scribe's Office, then transferred to Junior Imperial Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou took personal control of government, Fen was made Grand Master in the Inner Scribe's Office, then transferred to Junior Imperial Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 明習故事，每朝廷有所疑議，眾不能決者，芬輒為評斷，莫不稱善。

translations.literal: He was clear and practiced in precedent; whenever the court had doubtful points on which the multitude could not decide, Fen would judge and decide, and none failed to praise it as good.
translations.idiomatic: Expert in precedent, he was called on whenever the court faced a question the assembled officials could not settle; his rulings were invariably praised as sound.

sentences.zh: 後為司會。

translations.literal: He later became Director of Accounts.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Director of Accounts.

sentences.zh: 及申國公李穆討齊，引為行軍長史，封淮安縣男。

translations.literal: When Duke Li Mu of Shen campaigned against Qi, Fen was brought in as Chief Clerk on campaign and enfeoffed as Baron of Huai'an county.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Li Mu of Shen campaigned against Qi, Fen served as his chief clerk on campaign and was enfeoffed as Baron of Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 再遷東京小宗伯，鎮洛陽。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to Junior Grand Minister of Rites of the Eastern Capital and garrisoned Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Junior Grand Minister of Rites of the Eastern Capital and was stationed at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，尉遲迥與司馬消難陰謀往來，芬察知之，密白帝。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was Chancellor, Yuwen Jiong and Sima Xiaonan had secret dealings in conspiracy; Fen detected this and secretly reported to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was still chancellor, Fen discovered secret communications between Yuwen Jiong and Sima Xiaonan and reported them privately to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 由是深見親委，遷東京左僕射，進爵郡公。

translations.literal: Because of this he was deeply trusted and entrusted, moved to Left Vice Director of the Eastern Capital, and advanced in rank to Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For this he won deep trust, was made Left Vice Director of the Eastern Capital, and was advanced to duke of a commandery.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，罷東京官，拜尚書右僕射，與郢公王誼修律令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, the offices of the Eastern Capital were abolished; he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and, with Duke Wang Yi of Ying, revised the statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kaihuang era the Eastern Capital offices were abolished; Fen was appointed Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and joined Duke Wang Yi of Ying in revising the law code.

sentences.zh: 俄兼內史令，甚見信任。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Director of the Inner Scribe's Office and was greatly trusted.
translations.idiomatic: He soon held the additional post of Director of the Inner Scribe's Office and enjoyed the emperor's full confidence.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以老病出為蒲州刺史，加金紫光祿大夫，仍領關東運漕，賜錢百萬、粟五千石而遣之。

translations.literal: Before long, on account of age and illness he was sent out as Governor of Pu, given the additional title of Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and still directed transport of grain by water in Guandong; he was given a million cash and five thousand piculs of grain and sent off.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, citing age and illness, he was sent out as Governor of Pu with the additional title of Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and was left in charge of grain transport on the Guandong waterways; the emperor gave him a million cash and five thousand piculs of grain and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 後數年，上表乞骸骨，征還京師。

translations.literal: Several years later he submitted a memorial begging to surrender his bones and was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he petitioned to retire and was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 賜以三驥軺車，几杖被褥，歸於家。

translations.literal: He was given a three-horse light carriage, armrest, staff, bedding, and quilt, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a light carriage drawn by three fine horses, together with an armrest, staff, bedding, and quilts, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 皇太子又致巾帔。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince also sent him headcloth and kerchief.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince also sent him a headcloth and kerchief.

sentences.zh: 後數年，卒，帝遣使致祭，鴻臚監護喪事。

translations.literal: Several years later he died; the Emperor sent envoys to offer sacrifice, and the Director of Guests supervised the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: He died several years later; the emperor sent envoys to perform the sacrificial rites, and the Director of State Ceremonies oversaw the funeral.

sentences.zh: 子元恪嗣，位揚州總管司馬，左遷候衛長史。

translations.literal: His son Yuankuo succeeded him, holding the post of Chief Administrator under the Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou, then demoted to Chief Clerk of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuankuo succeeded him, serving as chief administrator under the Yangzhou commandery-in-chief before being demoted to chief clerk of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 少子元楷，與元恪皆明幹世事。

translations.literal: The younger son Yuankai, with Yuankuo, were both clear and capable in worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Yuankai, like Yuankuo, was sharp and capable in practical affairs.

sentences.zh: 元楷，大業中為曆陽郡丞，與廬江郡丞徐仲宗俱竭百姓之產，以貢於帝。

translations.literal: Yuankai, in the Daye era was Administrator of Liyang commandery; with the Administrator of Lujiang commandery Xu Zhongzong he both exhausted the people's wealth to present tribute to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign Yuankai served as administrator of Liyang commandery; he and Xu Zhongzong, administrator of Lujiang, both squeezed the people dry to send tribute to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 仲宗遷南郡丞；

translations.literal: Zhongzong was transferred to Administrator of Nan commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong was promoted to administrator of Nan commandery;

sentences.zh: 元楷超拜江都丞，兼領江都宮監。

translations.literal: Yuankai was promoted by special order to Administrator of Jiangdu and concurrently Superintendent of the Jiangdu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankai was specially promoted to administrator of Jiangdu and concurrently made superintendent of the Jiangdu palace.

sentences.zh: 王韶，字子相，自雲太原晉陽人也，世居京兆。

translations.literal: Wang Shao, styled Zixiang, claimed descent from Jinyang in Taiyuan, and his family had long resided in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao, whose courtesy name was Zixiang, claimed descent from Jinyang in Taiyuan, and his family had long lived in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖諧，原州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xie was Inspector of Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xie had served as Inspector of Yuan Province.

sentences.zh: 父諒，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Liang died young.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liang died while still young.

sentences.zh: 韶幼而方雅，頗好奇節，有識者異之。

translations.literal: From childhood Shao was upright and refined, took special delight in uncommon conduct, and those of discernment regarded him as unusual.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Shao was upright and refined, delighted in uncommon conduct, and men of discernment regarded him as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 在周，累以軍功，官至車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Under the Zhou he repeatedly won military merit and rose to Grand General of Agile Cavalry with the Honored Title Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he won repeated military honors and rose to Grand General of Agile Cavalry with the Honored Title Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 復轉軍正。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to serve as Army Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to serve as Army Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 周武帝既拔晉州，意欲旋師，韶諫曰：「取亂侮亡，正在今日。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wu of Zhou had taken Jin Prefecture and wished to withdraw the army, Shao remonstrated, saying: "To take advantage of disorder and insult the perishing—this is the moment.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Zhou had taken Jin Prefecture and wished to withdraw the army, Shao remonstrated: "To strike a disordered foe and trample a dying state—that moment is today.

sentences.zh: 方欲釋之而去，臣愚深所未解。」

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty now means to release them and depart—I deeply fail to understand this, your humble servant."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty now means to let them go and withdraw—I cannot understand it at all."

sentences.zh: 帝大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 及齊平，進位開府，封晉陽縣公，賜口馬雜畜萬計。

translations.literal: When Qi was pacified he was promoted to Opening Grandee, enfeoffed as Duke of Jinyang County, and given tens of thousands of head of livestock.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was pacified he was promoted to Opening Grandee, enfeoffed as Duke of Jinyang County, and given tens of thousands of head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 遷內史中大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Master of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，拜豐州刺史，改封昌樂縣公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded he was appointed Inspector of Feng Province and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Changle County.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded he was appointed Inspector of Feng Province and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Changle County.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，進爵項城郡公，轉靈州刺史，加位大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, Shao was advanced to Duke of Xiangcheng commandery, transferred to Governor of Ling, and given the additional rank of Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, Shao was advanced to Duke of Xiangcheng commandery, appointed Governor of Ling province, and given the additional rank of Grand General.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣之鎮并州，除行台右僕射，賜彩五百匹。

translations.literal: When Prince Jin Guang took up his post at Bingzhou, Shao was removed to be Right Vice Director of the Mobile Secretariat and given five hundred bolts of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jin Guang was posted to Bingzhou, Shao was made Right Vice Director of the mobile secretariat and given five hundred bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 韶性剛直，王甚憚之，每事諮詢，不敢違法度。

translations.literal: Shao's nature was upright and stern; the Prince greatly feared him, consulted him on every matter, and did not dare violate law and measure.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was upright and unyielding by nature; the prince held him in considerable awe, consulted him on every matter, and did not dare overstep the law.

sentences.zh: 韶嘗奉使檢行長城，後王穿池，起三山，韶既還，自鎖而諫，王謝而罷之。

translations.literal: Shao once went on mission to inspect the Long Wall; afterward the Prince dug a pond and raised three mountains; when Shao returned he locked himself in chains to remonstrate, and the Prince apologized and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while Shao was away on an inspection tour of the Great Wall, the prince dug a pond and built three artificial hills; when Shao returned he put himself in chains to remonstrate, and the prince apologized and abandoned the project.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而嘉歎，賜金百兩，並後宮四人。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and praised and sighed, giving a hundred taels of gold and four women from the rear palace besides.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of it with admiration and rewarded him with a hundred taels of gold and four women from the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，以本官為元帥府司馬。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Chen, with his original office he served as Chief Administrator in the Commander-in-Chief's Office.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign to conquer Chen he served in his existing rank as chief administrator on the commander-in-chief's staff.

sentences.zh: 及克金陵，韶即鎮焉。

translations.literal: When Jinling was taken, Shao immediately garrisoned there.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Jinling fell, Shao took command of the garrison there.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣班師，留韶於石頭防遏，委以後事。

translations.literal: Prince Jin Guang withdrew the army and left Shao at Shitou to guard and check, entrusting him with subsequent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jin Guang withdrew his army, he left Shao at Shitou to hold the line and entrusted him with all remaining affairs.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，征還。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 帝謂公卿曰：「晉王以幼出籓，遂能克平吳、越，王子相之力也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to the dukes and ministers, "Prince Jin, going out to a fief while young, was able to conquer and pacify Wu and Yue—this was the strength of a prince and his minister."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his ministers, "Prince Jin went to his fief while still young, yet he was able to subdue Wu and Yue—that was the work of a worthy prince and a capable minister."

sentences.zh: 於是進位柱國，賜奴婢三百口，錦絹五千段。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was advanced to Pillar of State, given three hundred slave servants, and five thousand lengths of brocade and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was thereupon promoted to Pillar of State and given three hundred household slaves and five thousand lengths of brocade and silk.

sentences.zh: 及上幸并州，以其稱職，特加勞勉。

translations.literal: When the sovereign visited Bingzhou, because Shao fulfilled his duties well, he was specially given encouragement and consolation.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Bingzhou, he singled Shao out for special praise and encouragement for his faithful service.

sentences.zh: 後上謂曰：「自朕至此，公須鬢漸白，無乃憂勞所致？

translations.literal: Later the sovereign said to him, "Since I came here, your beard and temples have gradually whitened—is it not caused by worry and toil?
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor said to him, "Since I arrived here your temples have turned noticeably gray—surely that comes from worry and overwork?

sentences.zh: 柱石之望，唯在於公，努力勉之！」

translations.literal: The hope of the pillar and stone rests on you alone—strive and exert yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: The empire's hopes rest on you alone—do your utmost!"

sentences.zh: 韶辭謝，上勞而遣之。

translations.literal: Shao declined with thanks; the sovereign comforted him and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Shao thanked him and withdrew; the emperor praised him once more and let him go.

sentences.zh: 秦王俊為并州總管，仍為長史。

translations.literal: When Prince Qin Jun served as Commander-in-Chief of Bingzhou, Shao remained as chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Qin Jun was Commander-in-Chief of Bingzhou, Shao continued to serve as his chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，馳驛入京，勞弊而卒。

translations.literal: After more than a year he sped to the capital by relay post, was worn out by the journey, and died.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he raced to the capital by relay post, was exhausted by the journey, and died.

sentences.zh: 帝甚傷惜之，謂秦王使者曰：「語爾王，我前令子相緩來，如何乃遣馳驛？

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply grieved and said to Prince Qin's messenger: "Tell your prince—I had earlier ordered Zixiang to come at an easy pace; why did he send him by relay post?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply grieved and said to Prince Qin's messenger, "Tell your prince: I had ordered Zixiang to come at an easy pace—why did you send him racing by relay post?

sentences.zh: 殺我子相，豈不由汝！」

translations.literal: You have killed my Zixiang—is this not your doing!"
translations.idiomatic: You have killed my Zixiang—is this not your fault!"

sentences.zh: 言甚冫妻愴。

translations.literal: His words were deeply sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: His words were deeply sorrowful.

sentences.zh: 使有司為立宅，曰：「往者何用宅為？

translations.literal: He ordered the authorities to build a residence and said: "What use is a house for the departed?
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the authorities to build a residence and said, "What use is a house for the departed?

sentences.zh: 但以表我深心耳！」

translations.literal: It is only to show the depth of my feelings!"
translations.idiomatic: It is only to show the depth of my feelings!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「子相受我委寄，十有餘年，終始不易。

translations.literal: He also said: "Zixiang bore my trust for more than ten years, constant from first to last.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Zixiang bore my trust for more than ten years, steadfast from first to last.

sentences.zh: 寵章未極，舍我而死乎！」

translations.literal: His honors had not yet reached their height—yet he left me and died!"
translations.idiomatic: His honors had not yet reached their height—yet he left me and died!"

sentences.zh: 發言流涕。

translations.literal: As he spoke, tears streamed down.
translations.idiomatic: As he spoke, tears streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 因命取子相封事數十紙，傳示群臣曰：「其真言匡正，裨益甚多，吾每披尋，未嘗釋手。」

translations.literal: He then ordered Zixiang's sealed memorials, several tens of sheets, brought forth and shown to the ministers, saying: "His sincere words correct and improve affairs in many ways; whenever I read through them I never lay them aside."
translations.idiomatic: He then had several tens of sheets of Zixiang's sealed memorials brought forth and shown to the ministers, saying, "His sincere words correct and improve affairs in many ways; whenever I read through them I never lay them aside."

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，追贈司徒、尚書令、靈豳等十州刺史、魏公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded he posthumously granted Shao the titles of Minister of Education, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Inspector of the ten provinces including Ling and Bin, and Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded he posthumously granted Shao the titles of Minister of Education, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Inspector of the ten provinces including Ling and Bin, and Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 子士隆嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shilong succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shilong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 士隆略知書計，尤便弓馬，慷慨有父風。

translations.literal: Shilong had some knowledge of writing and reckoning, was especially skilled with bow and horse, and was generous and bold with his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong had some schooling in letters and accounts, excelled above all at archery and horsemanship, and was generous and bold in his father's mold.

sentences.zh: 大業世，頗見親重，位備身將軍，改封耿國公。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he was rather favored and honored, holding the post of General of the Personal Guard, and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Geng.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign he enjoyed considerable favor, rose to General of the Personal Guard, and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Geng.

sentences.zh: 越王侗稱帝，士隆率數千兵自江淮而至。

translations.literal: When Prince Yue of the East Tong declared himself emperor, Shilong led several thousand troops from the Jiang-Huai and arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yue of the East, Yang Tong, declared himself emperor, Shilong led several thousand men from the Jiang-Huai region to join him.

sentences.zh: 會王世充僭號，甚禮重之，署尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Shichong usurped the title; he greatly honored and esteemed Shilong and appointed him Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong had by then declared himself emperor; he treated Shilong with great respect and made him Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 憂憤，疽發背卒。

translations.literal: Grieved and indignant, a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Tormented by grief and anger, he developed a carbuncle on his back and died.

sentences.zh: 元巖，字君山，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Yan, styled Junshan, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yan, whose courtesy name was Junshan, came from Luoyang in Henan commandery.

sentences.zh: 父禎，魏敷州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Zhen was Governor of Fuzhou in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhen had been Governor of Fu under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 岩好讀書，不守章名，剛鯁有器局，以名節自許，少與勃海高熲、太原王韶同志友善。

translations.literal: Yan loved reading books and did not cling to chapter titles and names; he was upright and unyielding with capacity and vision, pledged himself by reputation and integrity, and in youth was of one will and friendly with Gao Bin of Bohai and Wang Shao of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan loved learning but cared little for formal titles; upright and strong-willed, he held himself to a standard of integrity and in youth was close friends with Gao Bin of Bohai and Wang Shao of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 仕周，為武賁給事。

translations.literal: He served Zhou as Attendant in the Martial Retinue.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he served as an attendant in the martial guard.

sentences.zh: 大塚宰宇文護見而器之，以為中外記室。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Yuwen Hu saw him and valued his talent, appointing him clerk for internal and external affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Yuwen Hu took notice of him and esteemed his ability, making him secretary for both court and field affairs.

sentences.zh: 累遷內史中大夫，封昌國縣伯。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became Palace Secretary Grand Master and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changguo county.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Palace Secretary Grand Master and was created Marquis of Changguo.

sentences.zh: 周宣帝嗣位，為政昏暴，京兆郡丞樂運輿櫬詣朝堂，陳帝八失，言甚切至。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan of Zhou succeeded to the throne, his government was benighted and violent; Yue Yun, Assistant Magistrate of Jingzhao commandery, came to the court hall bearing a coffin and set forth eight faults of the emperor, his words extremely pointed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan of Zhou came to the throne, his rule turned cruel and erratic. Yue Yun, deputy magistrate of Jingzhao, appeared at court carrying a coffin and laid out eight failings of the emperor in language sharp and unsparing.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，將戮之，朝臣莫有救者。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and was about to execute him; none among the court ministers dared rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and was on the point of putting him to death, yet not one minister at court would speak for him.

sentences.zh: 巖謂人曰：「臧洪同日，尚可俱死，其況比干乎？

translations.literal: Yan said to others: "Zang Hong on the same day could still die together — how much more so Bi Gan?
translations.idiomatic: Yan told those around him, "When Zang Hong asked to die on the same day as Chen Shi, they could still perish together — how much more is that true of Bi Gan?

sentences.zh: 若樂運不免，吾將與之俱斃。」

translations.literal: If Yue Yun is not spared, I shall die with him."
translations.idiomatic: If Yue Yun is not spared, I mean to die at his side."

sentences.zh: 詣閤請見，言於帝曰：「樂運知書奏必死，所以不顧身命者，欲取後世名。

translations.literal: He went to the gate and requested audience, saying to the emperor: "Yue Yun knew that submitting a memorial would mean death; the reason he did not spare his own life was that he wished to win a name for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the palace gate and asked to be received, then said to the emperor, "Yue Yun knew his memorial would cost him his life. He risked everything only to win a name that would outlive him.

sentences.zh: 陛下若殺之，乃成其名，落其術內。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty kills him, you will merely make his name and fall into his stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty executes him, you only fulfill his fame and walk straight into his design.

sentences.zh: 不如勞而遣之，以廣聖度。」

translations.literal: Better to reward him with labor and send him away, to broaden your sagely magnanimity."
translations.idiomatic: Better to acknowledge his effort and let him go, and so display the breadth of your imperial grace."

sentences.zh: 運因獲免。

translations.literal: Yue Yun was thus spared.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yun was spared as a result.

sentences.zh: 後帝將誅烏丸軌，岩不肯署詔。

translations.literal: Later, when the emperor was about to execute Wuhuan Gui, Yan refused to countersign the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor intended to put Wuhuan Gui to death, Yan would not put his name to the edict.

sentences.zh: 御正顏之儀切諫不入，巖進繼之，脫巾頓顙，三拜三進。

translations.literal: Director of Imperial Correctness Yan Zhiyi remonstrated urgently but could not get through; Yan advanced and continued the remonstrance, removed his cap and knocked his forehead on the ground, bowing three times and advancing three times.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhiyi, Director of Imperial Correctness, pleaded urgently in vain; Yan stepped forward to take up the remonstrance, removed his cap, and prostrated himself, bowing three times and pressing forward three times.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「汝欲党烏丸軌耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Do you wish to factionalize with Wuhuan Gui?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Are you taking Wuhuan Gui's side?"

sentences.zh: 岩曰：「臣非黨軌，正恐濫誅，失天下望。」

translations.literal: Yan said: "Your servant is not befriending Gui; I only fear indiscriminate execution and the loss of the world's hope."
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, "I am not siding with Gui. I fear only that reckless executions will cost Your Majesty the trust of the realm."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，使閹豎搏其面，遂廢於家。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and had eunuch attendants strike his face; he was then dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in his anger had eunuchs beat his face, and Yan was stripped of office and sent home.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，加開府、戶部中大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, Yan was additionally made Director of a Separate Office and Grand Master of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Wen of Sui still served as chief minister, Yan was given the rank of Separate Office Director and made Grand Master of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，拜兵部尚書，進爵平昌郡公。

translations.literal: When the throne was received, he was appointed Minister of War and advanced in rank to Duke of Pingchang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the abdication and accession, he was appointed Minister of War and raised to Duke of Pingchang.

sentences.zh: 巖性嚴重，明達世務，每有奏議，侃然正色，廷爭面折，無所回避，上及公卿皆敬憚之。

translations.literal: Yan's nature was stern and grave; clear-sighted in worldly affairs, whenever he had memorials or proposals he spoke forthrightly with upright countenance, disputing at court and rebutting to one's face without evasion; the emperor and all the high ministers both respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and dignified by nature, Yan understood the affairs of the age. In every memorial and proposal he spoke with unflinching candor, arguing in open court and contradicting men to their faces without shrinking; emperor and ministers alike respected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 時帝懲周代諸侯微弱，以致滅亡，由是分王諸子，權侔王室，以為磐石之固。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor, taking warning from the weakness of the Zhou feudatories that had led to extinction, thereupon enfeoffed his sons as kings with authority equal to the royal house, thinking to make a foundation solid as bedrock.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had taken warning from how the enfeebled feudal lords of the Zhou had invited ruin, and so enfeoffed his sons as kings with powers rivaling the throne itself, trusting that they would serve as an immovable bulwark.

sentences.zh: 遣晉王廣鎮并州，蜀王秀鎮益州。

translations.literal: He sent Prince of Jin Yang Guang to garrison Bingzhou and Prince of Shu Yang Xiu to garrison Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He posted Prince of Jin Yang Guang at Bingzhou and Prince of Shu Yang Xiu at Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 二王年並幼，選貞良有重望者為之僚佐。

translations.literal: Both princes were still young in years, so upright men of heavy reputation were chosen as their staff.
translations.idiomatic: Both princes were still young, so men of proven integrity and high standing were chosen to serve as their advisers.

sentences.zh: 時嚴與王韶為河北道行台右僕射，帝謂曰：「公宰相大器，今屈輔我兒，亦如曹參相齊之意。」

translations.literal: At that time Yan and Wang Shao were Right Vice Directors of the Hebei Circuit Office; the emperor said to them: "You are material for chief ministers; now you humbly assist my son, just as in the meaning of Cao Shen governing Qi."
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Wang Shao were then Right Vice Directors on the Hebei circuit staff. The emperor told them, "You are men fit for the highest office. That you now serve my son in a lesser post is like Cao Shen's governing of Qi — a deliberate restraint for the good of the state."

sentences.zh: 及巖到官，法令明肅，吏人稱焉。

translations.literal: When Yan arrived at his post, laws and orders were clear and strict, and officials and people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yan took up his post, his laws were clear and his discipline firm, and officials and common people alike praised him.

sentences.zh: 蜀王好奢，嘗欲取獠口為閹人，又欲生剖死囚，取膽為樂。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shu loved extravagance; he once wished to take Lao captives as eunuchs, and also wished to cut open condemned prisoners while alive and take their gall for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shu was fond of luxury. He once proposed taking captive Lao tribesmen for castration, and at another time wished to vivisect condemned prisoners and extract their gall bladders for sport.

sentences.zh: 巖皆不奉教，排閣切諫，王輒謝而止。

translations.literal: Yan in every case did not obey the orders; bursting through the gate he remonstrated urgently, and the prince would apologize and desist.
translations.idiomatic: Yan refused every such order, forcing his way in to remonstrate bluntly, whereupon the prince would apologize and abandon the plan.

sentences.zh: 憚巖為人，每循法度。

translations.literal: Fearing Yan's character, he each time followed law and measure.
translations.idiomatic: In awe of Yan's moral force, the prince thereafter kept to the bounds of law.

sentences.zh: 蜀中獄訟，巖所裁斷，莫不悅服。

translations.literal: In the prisons and lawsuits of Shu, those Yan judged none failed to be pleased and submit.
translations.idiomatic: In every prison case and lawsuit Yan decided in Shu, none went away dissatisfied.

sentences.zh: 有得罪者，謂曰：「平昌公與罪，吾何怨焉？」

translations.literal: One who had been punished said: "The Duke of Pingchang gave me my punishment — what grievance have I?"
translations.idiomatic: One man who had been punished said, "It was the Duke of Pingchang who judged me — what cause have I to resent him?"

sentences.zh: 上甚嘉之，賞賜優洽。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly praised this and rewarded him generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and rewarded him with exceptional generosity.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，上悼惜久之。

translations.literal: He died in office; the emperor mourned and regretted it for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office, and the emperor mourned his loss for a long while.

sentences.zh: 益州父老莫不隕涕，於今思之。

translations.literal: The elders of Yizhou none failed to shed tears; even to this day they remember him.
translations.idiomatic: The elders of Yizhou wept without exception, and remember him to this day.

sentences.zh: 巖卒後，蜀王為非法，造渾天儀，又共妃出獵，以彈彈人，多捕山獠充宦者，僚佐無能諫止。

translations.literal: After Yan died, the Prince of Shu committed unlawful acts: he built an armillary sphere, went hunting with his consort, used a slingshot to shoot people, and captured many mountain Lao to serve as palace eunuchs; none among his staff could remonstrate and stop him.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan's death the Prince of Shu gave himself over to lawlessness. He built an armillary sphere, hunted with his consort, shot people for sport with a pellet bow, and seized mountain Lao to fill the ranks of his eunuchs — and none of his staff could check him.

sentences.zh: 及秀得罪，上曰：「元巖若在，吾兒豈有是乎！」

translations.literal: When Xiu fell into guilt, the emperor said: "If Yuan Yan were still alive, would my son have come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu was punished, the emperor said, "Had Yuan Yan still been alive, my son would never have come to this!"

sentences.zh: 子弘嗣。

translations.literal: His son Hongsi succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongsi carried on his line.

sentences.zh: 歷給事郎、司朝謁者、北平通守。

translations.literal: He successively served as Attendant Gentleman, Court Herald of the Morning Audience, and Prefect of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Attendant Gentleman, Court Herald, and Prefect of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 宇文㢸

translations.literal: Yu Wenbi
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenbi

sentences.zh: 宇文㢸，字公輔，河南洛陽人也，其先與周同出。

translations.literal: Yu Wenbi, styled Gongfu, was a man of Luoyang in Henan; his ancestors shared a common origin with the Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenbi, whose courtesy name was Gongfu, came from Luoyang in Henan. His clan traced its descent from the same line as the Zhou royal house.

sentences.zh: 祖直力勤，魏钜鹿太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhiliqin was Administrator of Julu in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhiliqin had been Administrator of Julu under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 父珍，周宕州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Zhen was Governor of Dangzhou under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhen had served as Governor of Dang under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 㢸慷慨有大節，博學多通。

translations.literal: Wenbi was magnanimous and possessed of great integrity; broadly learned and master of many fields.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbi was openhanded and resolute, a man of broad learning and wide competence.

sentences.zh: 仕周，嘗奉使鄧至國及黑水、龍涸諸羌，前後降附三十餘部。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou, he was once sent on mission to the state of Dengzhi and to the Black Water, Longge, and other Qiang tribes; before and after, more than thirty groups submitted and attached themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he served on embassy to the state of Dengzhi and to the Black Water, Longge, and other Qiang peoples, and in the course of these missions brought more than thirty tribes to submission.

sentences.zh: 及還，奉詔修定五禮，書成奏之，賜田二頃、粟百石。

translations.literal: When he returned, he received an edict to revise and fix the Five Rites; when the book was completed he submitted it and was granted two qing of fields and a hundred shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was ordered to revise the Five Rites. When the work was finished and presented, he was granted two qing of land and a hundred shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 累遷小吏部，擢八人為縣令，皆有異績，世以為知人。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached the Junior Ministry of Personnel; he elevated eight men to county magistrate, all of whom had outstanding achievements, and the age considered him one who knew men.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the Junior Ministry of Personnel and promoted eight men to county magistracies, each of whom distinguished himself in office; the world judged him a keen judge of talent.

sentences.zh: 轉內史都上士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Senior Clerk of the Interior Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of Senior Clerk in the Interior Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武帝將謀出兵河陽以伐齊，㢸進策曰：「齊氏建國，於今累世，雖曰無道，尚有其人。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was about to plan sending troops from Heyang to attack Qi; Wenbi submitted a strategy saying: "The Qi house has established its state through many generations to this day; though called without the Way, it still has its men.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu planned to march from Heyang against Qi, Wenbi submitted a strategy: "The Qi regime has stood for generations. However corrupt it may be, it still has capable men.

sentences.zh: 今若用兵，須擇其地。

translations.literal: If we now use troops, we must choose the ground.
translations.idiomatic: If we commit forces now, we must choose our ground with care.

sentences.zh: 河陽要衝，精兵所聚，盡力攻圍，恐難得志。

translations.literal: Heyang is a strategic choke point where elite troops gather; if we exhaust our strength in siege and assault, I fear we shall hardly achieve our aim.
translations.idiomatic: Heyang is a vital crossing where elite troops are massed. To throw our full strength into a siege there is unlikely to succeed.

sentences.zh: 彼汾之曲，戍小山平，攻之易拔，用武之地也。」

translations.literal: There where the Fen River bends, the garrisons are small and the hills level; attacking there it is easy to seize, a place for employing military force."
translations.idiomatic: At the bend of the Fen, the garrisons are thin and the ground level — easy to overrun, and ground made for war."

sentences.zh: 帝不納，師竟無功。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept it; the army in the end achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected the advice, and the campaign came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 建德五年，大舉伐齊，卒用弼策。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiande, a great campaign was launched against Qi, and in the end Bi's strategy was used.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jiande a full-scale invasion of Qi was launched, and in the end Yu Wenbi's strategy was adopted.

sentences.zh: 於是募三輔豪俠少年數百人為別陽，從帝攻拔晉州，身被三瘡，苦戰不息，帝奇而壯之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he recruited several hundred bold young men of the Three Adjuncts as a separate command, followed the emperor in storming and taking Jinzhou, received three wounds on his body, fought bitterly without ceasing, and the emperor marveled at and praised his valor.
translations.idiomatic: He then recruited several hundred bold young men from the Three Adjuncts into a separate detachment, followed the emperor in the capture of Jinzhou, took three wounds in hard fighting without slackening, and the emperor admired his fierce courage.

sentences.zh: 因從平齊，以功拜上儀同，封武威縣公。

translations.literal: He then followed in the pacification of Qi and, for his merit, was appointed Senior Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Duke of Wuwei county.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to help pacify Qi and, for his service, was made Senior Pillar of State and created Duke of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，為守廟大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, he became Keeper of the Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, he was appointed Keeper of the Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 時突厥寇甘州，帝令侯莫陳昶擊之。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks raided Ganzhou; the emperor ordered Houmo Chen Chang to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks raided Ganzhou, the emperor sent Houmo Chen Chang against them.

sentences.zh: 㢸為監軍，謂昶曰：「宜選精騎，直趨祈連之西。

translations.literal: Wenbi served as army overseer and said to Chang: "You should select elite cavalry and strike straight toward the west of Qilian.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbi served as army overseer and told Chang, "Select your best horsemen and ride straight for the country west of the Qilian range.

sentences.zh: 賊若收軍，必自蓼泉之北，此地險隘，兼下濕，度其人馬，三日方度。

translations.literal: If the bandits withdraw their army, they must pass north of Liaoyuan; that ground is narrow and perilous, and moreover low and wet — estimating their men and horses, three days are needed to cross it.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy withdraws, they must come north of Liaoyuan — ground that is narrow, treacherous, and boggy. By my reckoning, men and horses would need three days to cross it.

sentences.zh: 彼勞我逸，破之必矣。

translations.literal: They weary while we rest; breaking them is certain.
translations.idiomatic: They would be exhausted while we were fresh — a certain victory.

sentences.zh: 若邀此路，真上策也。」

translations.literal: If we intercept this route, it is truly the superior strategy."
translations.idiomatic: To ambush them on that road would be the best plan of all."

sentences.zh: 昶不能用，西取合黎，大軍行遲，虜已出塞。

translations.literal: Chang could not use it; he went west by way of Heli, the great army marched slowly, and the barbarians had already left the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: Chang would not follow the advice. He marched west by Heli, the main force moved too slowly, and the enemy was already beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 其年，㢸又從梁士彥攻拔壽陽，改封安樂縣公，除澮州刺史，轉南司州刺史。

translations.literal: That same year Wenbi again followed Liang Shiyan in storming and taking Shouyang; his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Anle county, he was appointed Governor of Huaizhou, and was transferred to Governor of Southern Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Wenbi again followed Liang Shiyan in the capture of Shouyang. He was re-created Duke of Anle, appointed Governor of Huaizhou, and then transferred to Governor of Southern Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 司馬消難之奔陳，㢸追之不及。

translations.literal: When Sima Xiaonan fled to Chen, Wenbi pursued but could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Xiaonan fled to Chen, Wenbi pursued but failed to catch him.

sentences.zh: 遇陳將樊毅，戰於漳口，自旦及午，三戰三捷。

translations.literal: He encountered the Chen general Fan Yi and fought at Zhangkou; from dawn until noon they fought three battles and won three victories.
translations.idiomatic: He met the Chen general Fan Yi at Zhangkou and fought from dawn until noon, winning three engagements in succession.

sentences.zh: 除黃州刺史，轉南定州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Huangzhou and transferred to Governor of Southern Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Governor of Huangzhou and then transferred to Governor of Southern Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，以前功封平昌縣公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, for his earlier merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingchang county.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang era he was created Duke of Pingchang for his earlier service.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He entered court as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時西羌內附，詔㢸持節安集，置鹽澤、蒲昌二郡而還。

translations.literal: At that time the Western Qiang submitted internally; an edict ordered Wenbi to bear the staff of authority and settle and gather them, establishing the two commanderies of Yanze and Puchang, then returning.
translations.idiomatic: When the Western Qiang submitted, Wenbi was ordered to bear imperial credentials and pacify them. He established the commanderies of Yanze and Puchang and then returned.

sentences.zh: 遷左丞，當官正色，為百僚所憚。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Vice Director; upright in office and countenance, he was feared by the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Left Vice Director, he held himself with stern integrity in office and was feared by the entire bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 三年，突厥寇甘州，以行軍司馬元帥竇榮定擊破之。

translations.literal: In the third year the Turks raided Ganzhou; as army marching marshal under supreme commander Dou Rongding he defeated and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when the Turks raided Ganzhou, he served as army marching marshal under supreme commander Dou Rongding and routed them.

sentences.zh: 還除太僕少卿，轉吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: On returning he was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Stud and transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Vice Director of the Imperial Stud and then Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役。

translations.literal: The campaign to pacify Chen.
translations.idiomatic: During the conquest of Chen.

sentences.zh: 楊素出信州道，令㢸持節為諸軍節度，仍領行軍總管。

translations.literal: Yang Su marched by the Xizhou route; Wenbi was ordered to bear the staff as commander over the various armies, and still headed the campaigning grand general.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su advanced by the Xizhou route and appointed Wenbi to bear imperial credentials as overall commander of the forces, while retaining his post as campaigning grand general.

sentences.zh: 劉仁恩之破陳將呂仲肅也，㢸有謀焉。

translations.literal: In Liu Ren'en's defeat of the Chen general Lu Zhongsu, Wenbi had a hand in the planning.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Ren'en defeated the Chen general Lu Zhongsu, Wenbi had contributed to the strategy.

sentences.zh: 加開府，擢拜刑部尚書，領太子虞候率。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Director of a Separate Office, promoted and appointed Minister of Justice, and concurrently held the post of Chief Warden of the Crown Prince's Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the rank of Separate Office Director, promoted to Minister of Justice, and appointed Chief Warden of the Crown Prince's Retainers as well.

sentences.zh: 上嘗親臨釋奠。

translations.literal: The emperor once personally attended the libation ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once attended the Confucian sacrifice in person.

sentences.zh: 㢸與博士論議，詞致清遠。

translations.literal: Wenbi debated with the Erudites; his language was clear and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbi joined the Erudites in debate, his speech lucid and elevated.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，謂群臣曰：「朕今睹周公之制禮，見宣尼之論孝，實慰朕心。」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said to the assembled ministers: "Today I behold the Duke of Zhou's establishment of rites and see Confucius's discourse on filial piety — it truly comforts my heart."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and told the assembled ministers, "Today I have seen the Duke of Zhou's ordering of ritual and Confucius's teaching on filial piety — and my heart is deeply eased."

sentences.zh: 時朝廷以晉陽為重鎮，并州總管必屬親王，其長史、司馬亦一時高選。

translations.literal: At that time the court regarded Jinyang as a heavy stronghold; the Area Commander of Bingzhou must belong to an imperial prince, and his Chief Administrator and Army Marshal were also chosen from the highest talent of the age.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court treated Jinyang as a strategic stronghold. The Area Commander of Bingzhou was always an imperial prince, and his chief administrator and army marshal were chosen from the finest men of the day.

sentences.zh: 前長史王韶卒，以㢸有文武幹用，出為并州長史。

translations.literal: The former Chief Administrator Wang Shao died; because Wenbi had civil and military capacity and usefulness, he was sent out as Chief Administrator of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the former chief administrator Wang Shao died, Wenbi was sent out as Chief Administrator of Bingzhou for his proven ability in both civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遼東之役，授元帥漢王府司馬，仍領行軍總管。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, in the Liaodong campaign, he was appointed Army Marshal to the Prince of Han's headquarters and still headed the campaigning grand general.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, during the Liaodong campaign, he was made army marshal on the staff of the Prince of Han while continuing to serve as campaigning grand general.

sentences.zh: 軍還，歷朔、代、吳三州總管，皆有能名。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he successively served as Area Commander of Shuozhou, Daizhou, and Wuzhou, all with reputations for ability.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned he served in turn as area commander of Shuozhou, Daizhou, and Wuzhou, earning a name for competence in each post.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，拜刑部尚書，仍持節，巡省河北。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Wenbi was appointed Minister of Justice, still bearing the staff, and toured and inspected Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, Wenbi was appointed Minister of Justice and sent with imperial credentials to inspect Hebei.

sentences.zh: 還除泉州刺史。

translations.literal: On returning he was appointed Governor of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Governor of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 復徵拜刑部尚書，轉禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was again summoned and appointed Minister of Justice, then transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and reappointed Minister of Justice, then transferred to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 㢸既以才能著稱，歷職顯要，聲望甚重，物議多見推許。

translations.literal: Wenbi had already become renowned for talent and ability; through offices of conspicuous importance his reputation was very weighty, and public opinion widely praised and approved him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbi was already famed for his ability. Having held one high office after another, he carried great weight in public esteem, and opinion widely favored him.

sentences.zh: 帝頗忌之。

translations.literal: The emperor was rather jealous of him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew wary of him.

sentences.zh: 時帝漸好聲色，尤勤遠略，㢸謂高熲曰：「昔周天元好聲色亡國，以今方之，不亦甚乎！」

translations.literal: At that time the emperor gradually favored music and women, and was especially zealous for distant campaigns; Wenbi said to Gao Bin: "Formerly Emperor Xuan of Northern Zhou loved music and women and lost the state — compared with today, is it not even worse!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was turning ever more to pleasure and grand distant campaigns. Wenbi said to Gao Bin, "When Emperor Xuan of Northern Zhou drowned in pleasure, the dynasty fell. Measured against that, are we not worse still?"

sentences.zh: 又言「長城之役，幸非急務」。

translations.literal: He also said, "The Great Wall labor is no urgent task."
translations.idiomatic: He also remarked, "The Great Wall project is no urgent necessity."

sentences.zh: 有人奏之，坐誅，天下冤之。

translations.literal: Someone memorialized this; he was punished with execution, and the realm considered it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported his words to the throne. He was executed for it, and the empire regarded his death as a grievous wrong.

sentences.zh: 所著辭賦二十餘萬言，為《尚書》、《孝經注》行於世。

translations.literal: His compositions in prose and rhapsody numbered more than two hundred thousand words; his commentaries on the Documents and the Classic of Filial Piety circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He left more than two hundred thousand words of prose and poetry, and his commentaries on the Documents and the Classic of Filial Piety circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 有子儉瑗。

translations.literal: He had a son Jianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Jianyuan.

sentences.zh: 伊婁謙

translations.literal: Yi Louqian
translations.idiomatic: Yi Louqian

sentences.zh: 伊婁謙，字彥恭，本鮮卑人也。

translations.literal: Yi Louqian, styled Yangong, was originally a Xianbei man.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Louqian, whose courtesy name was Yangong, was of Xianbei origin.

sentences.zh: 其先世為酋長，隨魏南遷。

translations.literal: His ancestors for generations were chieftains and followed the Wei in migrating south.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had been tribal chieftains who migrated south with the Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖信，中部太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xin was Administrator of Zhongbu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xin had been Administrator of Zhongbu.

sentences.zh: 父靈，相隆二州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Ling was Governor of the two provinces of Xiang and Long.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ling had served as governor of Xiang and Long provinces.

sentences.zh: 謙性忠直，善辭令。

translations.literal: Louqian's nature was loyal and upright; he was skilled in rhetoric and command of language.
translations.idiomatic: Louqian was loyal and forthright by nature, and gifted in speech.

sentences.zh: 仕周，累遷宣納上士、使持節、驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou, through successive promotions he became Senior Herald, Bearer of the Staff of Authority, and General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he rose to Senior Herald, Bearer of the Staff of Authority, and General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 武帝將伐齊，召入內殿，問以兵事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was about to attack Qi, he summoned him into the inner hall and questioned him on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu prepared to invade Qi, he summoned Louqian to the inner hall and questioned him on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「偽齊僭擅，跋扈不恭，沉溺倡優，耽昏曲蘖。

translations.literal: He replied: "The false Qi usurps and monopolizes power, overbearing and disrespectful, drowning in performers and entertainers, sunk in drunkenness and wine.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The usurper state of Qi is arrogant and insubordinate, drowning in singers and actors and lost in wine.

sentences.zh: 其折沖之將斛律明月已斃讒人之口，上下離心。

translations.literal: Its general who breaks the enemy's charge, Hulu Mingyue, has already perished at the mouths of slanderers; above and below are divided in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Its foremost general, Hulu Mingyue, has already been destroyed by slander, and court and army alike have lost heart.

sentences.zh: 若命六師齊進，臣之願也。」

translations.literal: If ordered, the six armies advance together — that is this subject's wish."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty orders the six armies to advance together, that is my dearest wish."

sentences.zh: 帝大笑，因使謙與小司寇拓跋偉聘齊觀釁。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed greatly and thereupon sent Louqian together with Vice Minister of Justice Tuoba Wei on a mission to Qi to observe signs of strife.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed heartily and sent Louqian with Vice Minister of Justice Tuoba Wei as envoys to Qi to watch for any opening.

sentences.zh: 帝尋發兵。

translations.literal: The Emperor soon launched troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon mobilized his armies.

sentences.zh: 齊主知之，令其僕射陽休之責謙曰：「貴朝盛夏徵兵，馬首何向？」

translations.literal: When the ruler of Qi learned of it, he had his Vice Chancellor Yang Xiuzhi reproach Louqian, saying: "Your honored court is conscripting troops in the height of summer — where do your horses' heads point?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi ruler learned of this, he had his Vice Chancellor Yang Xiuzhi reproach Louqian: "Your court is raising troops in the middle of summer — where are your armies headed?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「僕拭玉之始，未聞興師。

translations.literal: He replied: "Since this servant began polishing jade, I have not heard of raising armies.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Since I set out on this mission, I have heard nothing of any mobilization.

sentences.zh: 設復西增白帝之城，東益巴丘之戍，豈足怪哉！」

translations.literal: Even if you again bolster White Emperor City in the west and reinforce the garrison at Baqiu in the east, what is there to marvel at!"
translations.idiomatic: Even if you were to strengthen White Emperor City in the west and add troops to the garrison at Baqiu in the east, what would be so strange about that?"

sentences.zh: 謙參軍高遵以情輸齊，遂留謙不遣。

translations.literal: Louqian's staff officer Gao Zun divulged the facts to Qi, so they detained Louqian and would not send him back.
translations.idiomatic: Louqian's aide Gao Zun betrayed the mission to Qi, and the Qi court detained Louqian and refused to let him return.

sentences.zh: 帝既克并州，召謙勞之。

translations.literal: After the Emperor had taken Bingzhou, he summoned Louqian to commend him.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor captured Bingzhou, he summoned Louqian to reward him.

sentences.zh: 乃執遵付謙，任令報復，謙頓首請赦之。

translations.literal: He then seized Gao Zun and handed him over to Louqian, letting him take revenge as he wished; Louqian prostrated himself and begged that Gao be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Gao Zun seized and handed over to Louqian, telling him to take whatever revenge he chose; Louqian kowtowed and begged that Gao be spared.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿可聚眾唾面，令知愧也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You could gather the crowd to spit in his face and let him know shame."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You could have the whole company spit in his face and teach him shame."

sentences.zh: 謙跪曰：「遵罪又非唾面之責。」

translations.literal: Louqian knelt and said: "Gao Zun's offense is not one for which spitting in the face is the fitting punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Louqian knelt and said, "Gao Zun's crime is not one that calls for spitting in the face."

sentences.zh: 帝善其言而止。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his reply and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 謙竟待遵如初。

translations.literal: Louqian in the end treated Gao Zun just as before.
translations.idiomatic: Louqian continued to treat Gao Zun exactly as he had before.

sentences.zh: 尋賜爵濟陽縣伯，累遷前驅中大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was granted the title Baron of Jiyang County and was promoted in succession to Vanguard Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon enfeoffed as Baron of Jiyang County and rose in succession to Vanguard Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 大象中，進爵為侯，位開府。

translations.literal: During the Daxiang era, he was advanced to marquis and given the rank of Bearer of the Opening Office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daxiang reign, he was promoted to marquis and granted the rank of Bearer of the Opening Office.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝作相，授亳州總管，俄征還京。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui served as Chancellor, he was appointed Regional Commander of Bozhou; soon after he was recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui became Chancellor, Louqian was appointed Regional Commander of Bozhou, but was soon recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 恥與逆人王謙同名，因爾稱字。

translations.literal: Ashamed of sharing a name with the rebel Wang Qian, he thereafter used his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of sharing a name with the rebel Wang Qian, he thereafter went by his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 文帝受禪，以彥恭為左武候將軍，俄拜大將軍，進爵為公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen received the abdication, he appointed Yangong Left Martial Gate General; soon he was made Grand General and advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, he appointed Yangong Left Martial Gate General; soon afterward he was made Grand General and ennobled as a duke.

sentences.zh: 後出為澤州刺史，清約自處，甚得人和。

translations.literal: Later he went out as Governor of Ze Province, living plainly and frugally, and winning the people's affection exceedingly.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was sent out as Governor of Ze Province, where he lived plainly and frugally and won the people's deep affection.

sentences.zh: 以疾去職，吏人攀戀，行數百里不絕。

translations.literal: Because of illness he left office; officials and commoners clung to him in farewell, their procession continuing for several hundred li without break.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned because of illness; officials and commoners clung to him in farewell, and the procession of mourners stretched on for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 子傑嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jie succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jie succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 李圓通

translations.literal: Li Yuantong
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuantong

sentences.zh: 李圓通，京兆涇陽人也。

translations.literal: Li Yuantong was a man of Jingyang in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuantong was a native of Jingyang in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 少孤賤，給使隋文帝家。

translations.literal: Orphaned and lowly in youth, he served in the household of Emperor Wen of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and of humble birth, he served in the household of the future Emperor Wen of Sui.

sentences.zh: 及帝為隋公，擢授參軍事。

translations.literal: When the emperor became Duke of Sui, he was promoted and appointed as a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was enfeoffed as Duke of Sui, Yuantong was promoted and appointed a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 初，帝少時，每宴客，恆令圓通監廚。

translations.literal: In the beginning, when the emperor was young, whenever he entertained guests he always had Yuantong supervise the kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth, whenever Yang Jian entertained guests, he always put Yuantong in charge of the kitchen.

sentences.zh: 圓通性嚴整，左右婢僕，咸所敬憚。

translations.literal: Yuantong was stern and disciplined by nature; the servants and attendants on all sides both respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuantong was stern and exacting by nature, and all the servants and attendants both respected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 唯世子乳母恃寵輕之，賓客未供，每有幹請。

translations.literal: Only the crown prince's wet nurse, relying on favor, looked down on him; before the guests' food was ready, she would often make unauthorized requests.
translations.idiomatic: Only the crown prince's wet nurse, relying on her favor with the family, looked down on him and would make unauthorized demands before the guests' meal was ready.

sentences.zh: 圓通不許，或輒持去。

translations.literal: Yuantong would not permit it, but sometimes she would simply take things away.
translations.idiomatic: Yuantong refused, but sometimes she would simply take what she wanted.

sentences.zh: 圓通大怒，叱廚人撾之數十，叫聲徹於閣內，僚吏左右，代其失色。

translations.literal: Yuantong flew into a rage and ordered the kitchen staff to beat her several dozen times; her cries rang through the pavilion, and the officials and attendants present turned pale on her behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Yuantong flew into a rage and ordered the kitchen staff to beat her several dozen times; her screams rang through the hall, and the officials and attendants nearby turned pale on her account.

sentences.zh: 賓去後，帝知之，召圓通命坐賜食，從此獨善之，以為堪當大任。

translations.literal: After the guests had left, the emperor learned of it, summoned Yuantong, had him sit and bestowed food on him; from then on he favored him alone, thinking him fit for great responsibility.
