translations.idiomatic: After the guests had gone, Yang Jian learned what had happened, summoned Yuantong, had him sit and shared a meal with him, and from then on singled him out for favor, believing him fit for great responsibility.

sentences.zh: 帝作相，賜爵懷昌男。

translations.literal: When the emperor became Chancellor, he was granted the title Baron of Huaichang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became Chancellor, Yuantong was enfeoffed as Baron of Huaichang.

sentences.zh: 授帥都督，進爵新安子，委以心膂。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commander-in-Chief, advanced to Viscount of Xin'an, and entrusted as a trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Commander-in-Chief, promoted to Viscount of Xin'an, and entrusted as one of Yang Jian's closest confidants.

sentences.zh: 圓通多力勁捷，長於武用。

translations.literal: Yuantong was strong, vigorous, and agile, excelling in martial use.
translations.idiomatic: Yuantong was powerful, quick, and agile, and excelled in martial affairs.

sentences.zh: 周代諸王素憚帝，伺便圖為不利，賴圓通保護，獲免者數矣。

translations.literal: The princes of the Zhou had long feared the emperor and watched for chances to do him harm; thanks to Yuantong's protection, he escaped harm on numerous occasions.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou princes had long feared Yang Jian and watched for chances to do him harm; thanks to Yuantong's protection, he escaped danger many times.

sentences.zh: 帝深感之，由是參預政事，授相國外兵曹，仍領左親信。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply grateful to him and from this participated in government affairs; he was appointed External Military Affairs Officer of the Chancellor's Office and still headed the Left Personal Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian was deeply grateful and from then on brought him into state affairs, appointing him External Military Affairs Officer of the Chancellor's Office while keeping him in charge of the Left Personal Guard.

sentences.zh: 尋授上儀同。

translations.literal: Soon he was granted Senior Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon granted the rank of Senior Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 帝受禪，拜內史侍郎，領左衛長史，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the abdication, he was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, concurrently Chief Secretary of the Left Guard, and advanced to baron.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne, Yuantong was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Chief Secretary of the Left Guard, and was ennobled as a baron.

sentences.zh: 曆左右庶子、給事黃門侍郎、尚書左丞，攝刑部尚書，深被任信。

translations.literal: He served successively as Left and Right Supervisor of the Heir Apparent, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, acting as Minister of Justice — deeply trusted.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Supervisor of the Heir Apparent on both the left and right, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, also acting as Minister of Justice, and was deeply trusted.

sentences.zh: 伐陳之役，以行軍總管從楊素出信州道，以功進位大將軍。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Chen, he served as Mobile Campaign Commander following Yang Su along the Xinzhou route, and for his merit was promoted to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Chen, he served as Mobile Campaign Commander under Yang Su on the Xinzhou route and was promoted to Grand General for his merit.

sentences.zh: 改封萬安縣公，揚州總管長史。

translations.literal: His fief was changed to Duke of Wan'an County; he became Chief Secretary to the Regional Commander of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was changed to Duke of Wan'an County, and he became Chief Secretary to the Regional Commander of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 秦孝王仁柔自喜，少斷決，府中事多決於圓通。

translations.literal: Prince Xiao of Qin was benevolent, gentle, and self-satisfied, with little decisiveness; most affairs of his princely establishment were decided by Yuantong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao of Qin was mild, gentle, and self-satisfied, with little taste for decision, and most affairs of his household were settled by Yuantong.

sentences.zh: 入為司農卿，遷刑部尚書，後復為并州長史。

translations.literal: He entered court as Minister of Public Revenue, was transferred to Minister of Justice, and later again served as Chief Secretary of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Minister of Public Revenue, was transferred to Minister of Justice, and later served again as Chief Secretary of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝王以奢得罪，圓通亦坐免。

translations.literal: Prince Xiao was punished for extravagance, and Yuantong was also dismissed in connection with it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao was punished for extravagance, and Yuantong was dismissed along with him.

sentences.zh: 尋檢校刑部尚書事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed acting supervisor of the affairs of the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed acting supervisor of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，以勳舊進爵郡公。

translations.literal: During the Renshou era, as a meritorious elder he was advanced to Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou reign, as a veteran of merit he was promoted to commandery duke.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，拜兵部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he was appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Yuantong was appointed Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 帝幸揚州，以圓通留守京師。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Yangzhou, he had Yuantong remain behind to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled to Yangzhou, he left Yuantong behind to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 判宇文述田還百姓，述訴其受賂。

translations.literal: He ruled that Yuwen Shu's lands should be returned to the common people; Yuwen Shu accused him of taking bribes.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled that Yuwen Shu's lands should be returned to the common people, and Yuwen Shu accused him of taking bribes.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，坐是免官。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged and for this reason dismissed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and dismissed him from office on that account.

sentences.zh: 圓通憂懼發病，卒。

translations.literal: Yuantong, distressed and fearful, fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yuantong, stricken with anxiety and fear, fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 贈柱國，封爵悉如故。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Pillar of State; his titles and fiefs all remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Pillar of State, and his titles and fiefs were all left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 子孝常，大業末，為華陰令。

translations.literal: His son Xiaochang, at the end of the Daye era, was Magistrate of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaochang, in the final years of the Daye reign, served as Magistrate of Huayin.

sentences.zh: 武德初，以應義旗功，封義安王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, for merit in answering the righteous banner, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yi'an.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wude reign, for merit in rallying to the righteous banner, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yi'an.

sentences.zh: 又有陳茂者，河東猗氏人。

translations.literal: There was also a Chen Mao, a man of Yishi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a Chen Mao, a native of Yishi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 家世寒微，質直恭謹，為州裏所稱。

translations.literal: His family for generations was humble and lowly; he was plain, upright, respectful, and cautious, praised by his district and neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been poor and humble; he was plain, upright, respectful, and careful, and was praised throughout the district.

sentences.zh: 文帝為隋國公，引為僚佐，待遇與圓通等。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was Duke of the State of Sui, he recruited him as a staff officer, treating him the same as Yuantong and the like.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was Duke of the State of Sui, he took Chen Mao onto his staff and treated him the same as Yuantong and the others.

sentences.zh: 每令典家事，常稱旨。

translations.literal: Whenever he was put in charge of household affairs, he always accorded with the emperor's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yang Jian put him in charge of household affairs, he always carried out his wishes to the letter.

sentences.zh: 後從帝與齊師戰于晉州，賊甚盛，帝將挑戰，茂固止不得，因捉馬鞚。

translations.literal: Later he followed the emperor in battle against Qi forces at Jinzhou; the enemy was very strong, and as the emperor was about to offer battle, Mao firmly tried to stop him but could not, so he seized the horse's bridle.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Yang Jian into battle against Qi forces at Jinzhou; the enemy was very strong, and as Yang Jian was about to engage them, Mao tried desperately to stop him and, failing that, seized the horse's bridle.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，拔刀斫其額，流血被面，詞氣不撓。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious, drew his sword and struck his forehead; blood covered his face, yet his words and bearing did not falter.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian flew into a rage, drew his sword, and struck Mao on the forehead; blood covered his face, yet his words and bearing never faltered.

sentences.zh: 帝感而謝之，厚加禮敬。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved and apologized to him, treating him with great courtesy and respect.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian was moved and apologized to him, treating him thereafter with great courtesy and respect.

sentences.zh: 帝為丞相，委以心膂。

translations.literal: When the emperor became Chancellor, he entrusted him as a trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became Chancellor, he entrusted Chen Mao as one of his closest confidants.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，拜給事黃門侍郎，封魏城縣男，每典機密。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, Mao was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, enfeoffed as Baron of Weicheng County, and regularly handled confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne, Chen Mao was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, enfeoffed as Baron of Weicheng County, and regularly handled confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 轉益州總管司馬，遷太府卿，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Military Assistant to the Regional Commander of Yizhou, promoted to Minister of the Imperial Storehouse, and advanced to baron.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Military Assistant to the Regional Commander of Yizhou, promoted to Minister of the Imperial Storehouse, and ennobled as a baron.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子政嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zheng succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zheng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 政字弘道，倜儻有文武大略，善鐘律，便弓馬。

translations.literal: Zheng, courtesy name Hongdao, was bold and free-spirited with broad civil and military talent, skilled in pitch and regulation, adept at bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, whose courtesy name was Hongdao, was bold and unconventional, possessed of broad civil and military talent, skilled in music and pitch, and adept at archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 少養宮中，年十七，為太子千牛備身。

translations.literal: Raised in the palace from youth, at seventeen he became a Thousand-Ox Guard attendant to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Raised in the palace from childhood, he became a Thousand-Ox Guard attendant to the crown prince at seventeen.

sentences.zh: 京都大俠劉居士重政才氣，數從之遊。

translations.literal: Liu Jushi, a great chivalrous figure of the capital, valued Zheng's talent and spirit and often kept company with him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jushi, a famous man of the capital's underworld, admired Zheng's talent and spirit and often kept company with him.

sentences.zh: 圓通子孝常與政相善，並與居士交結。

translations.literal: Yuantong's son Xiaochang was on good terms with Zheng, and both also associated with Jushi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuantong's son Xiaochang was on good terms with Zheng, and both also became close to Jushi.

sentences.zh: 及居士伏誅，政及常從坐，上以功臣子，撻之二百而赦之。

translations.literal: When Jushi was executed, Zheng and Xiaochang were implicated; because they were sons of meritorious ministers, the emperor had them flogged two hundred strokes and then pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: When Jushi was executed, Zheng and Xiaochang were implicated along with him; because they were sons of meritorious ministers, the emperor had them flogged two hundred strokes and then pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 由是不得調。

translations.literal: For this reason they were not given official appointments.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason they were barred from official appointment.

sentences.zh: 煬帝時，歷位協律郎、通事謁者、兵曹承務郎。

translations.literal: During Emperor Yang's reign, he held in succession the posts of Director of Harmonic Regulation, Herald for Affairs, and Clerk in the Military Affairs Section.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Yang's reign, he served in succession as Director of Harmonic Regulation, Herald for Affairs, and Clerk in the Military Affairs Section.

sentences.zh: 帝以其才，甚重之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly valued him for his talent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly valued him for his talent.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之亂，以為太常卿。

translations.literal: During the rebellion of Yuwen Huaji, he was made Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuwen Huaji's rebellion, he was appointed Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 後歸大唐，為梁州總管，遇賊見殺。

translations.literal: Later he submitted to Great Tang and served as Regional Commander of Liangzhou; he encountered bandits and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he submitted to the Tang and served as Regional Commander of Liangzhou, where he was killed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 郭榮，字長榮，自雲太原人也。

translations.literal: Guo Rong, courtesy name Changrong, claimed to be a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Rong, whose courtesy name was Changrong, claimed Taiyuan as his ancestral home.

sentences.zh: 父徽，仕魏為同州司馬。

translations.literal: His father Hui served the Wei as Vice Governor of Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui served the Wei as Vice Governor of Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 時武元皇帝為刺史，由是與隋文帝有舊。

translations.literal: At that time the Wuyuan Emperor served as provincial governor, and through this he had old ties with Emperor Wen of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Wuyuan Emperor was serving as provincial governor, and through this connection the family formed old ties with the future Emperor Wen of Sui.

sentences.zh: 徽後位洵州刺史、安城縣公。

translations.literal: Hui later held the post of Governor of Xun Province and Duke of Ancheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Hui later served as Governor of Xun Province and was enfeoffed as Duke of Ancheng County.

sentences.zh: 及帝受禪，拜太僕卿，卒官。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the abdication, he was appointed Minister of Imperial Studs and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Hui was appointed Minister of Imperial Studs and died in office.

sentences.zh: 榮容貌魁岸，外疏內密，與交者多愛之。

translations.literal: Rong had a towering appearance; outwardly open but inwardly careful — many who associated with him came to love him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was imposing in appearance, open in manner but careful at heart, and many who knew him came to love him.

sentences.zh: 周大塚宰宇文護引為親信。

translations.literal: Yuwen Hu, Grand Chancellor of Zhou, recruited him as a personal confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu, Grand Chancellor of Zhou, took him on as a personal confidant.

sentences.zh: 護察榮謹願，擢為中外府水曹參軍。

translations.literal: Hu saw that Rong was careful and earnest and promoted him to Water Affairs Officer of the Central and Outer Office.
translations.idiomatic: Hu saw that Rong was careful and dutiful and promoted him to Water Affairs Officer of the Central and Outer Office.

sentences.zh: 齊寇屢侵，護令榮於汾州觀城勢，時汾州與姚襄鎮相去懸遠，榮以二城孤迥，勢不相救，請於州鎮間更築城以相控攝，護從之。

translations.literal: Qi raiders invaded repeatedly; Hu sent Rong to Fenzhou to observe the disposition of the walls. At the time Fenzhou and Yaoxiang Fort were far apart; Rong argued that the two cities stood isolated and apart and could not rescue each other, and requested that another city be built between province and fort to control and oversee the area. Hu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi raiders invaded repeatedly, Hu sent Rong to Fenzhou to inspect the fortifications. Fenzhou and Yaoxiang Fort were then far apart; Rong argued that the two posts stood too isolated to support each other and asked that a new fort be built between them to keep the area under control. Hu agreed.

sentences.zh: 俄而齊將段孝先攻陷姚襄、汾州二城，唯榮所立者獨能自守。

translations.literal: Before long the Qi general Duan Xiaoxian captured the two cities of Yaoxiang and Fenzhou; only the fort Rong had built could hold on its own.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Qi general Duan Xiaoxian captured both Yaoxiang and Fenzhou; only the fort Rong had built was able to hold.

sentences.zh: 護作浮橋出兵，孝先於上流縱大筏擊浮橋，護令榮督便水者引取其筏。

translations.literal: Hu built a pontoon bridge to deploy troops; Xiaoxian released great rafts upstream to strike the bridge, and Hu ordered Rong to supervise the skilled watermen in capturing those rafts.
translations.idiomatic: Hu built a pontoon bridge to move troops across the river; Xiaoxian sent great rafts downstream to smash it, and Hu ordered Rong to supervise the skilled watermen in seizing the rafts.

sentences.zh: 以功授大都督。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was appointed Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 護又以稽胡數為寇亂，使綏集之。

translations.literal: Hu also assigned him to pacify and assemble the Ji Hu, who repeatedly raided and caused disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Hu also put him in charge of pacifying the Ji Hu, who had repeatedly raided and caused disorder.

sentences.zh: 榮于上郡、延安築周昌、弘信、廣安、招遠、咸寧等五城以遏其要路，稽胡由是不能為寇。

translations.literal: Rong built at Shang Commandery and Yan'an the five forts Zhoucheng, Hongxin, Guang'an, Zhaoyuan, and Xianning to block their key routes, so that from then on the Ji Hu could not raid.
translations.idiomatic: Rong built five forts at Shang Commandery and Yan'an — Zhoucheng, Hongxin, Guang'an, Zhaoyuan, and Xianning — to block their key routes, and from then on the Ji Hu could no longer raid.

sentences.zh: 周武親總萬機，拜宣納中士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou personally directed all affairs of state, Rong was appointed Master of Proclamation and Reception.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou personally took charge of government, Rong was appointed Master of Proclamation and Reception.

sentences.zh: 後從平齊，以功封平陽縣男。

translations.literal: Later he followed the campaign to pacify Qi and for his merit was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Later he took part in the conquest of Qi and was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingyang County for his merit.

sentences.zh: 遷司水大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of Waterworks.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of Grand Master of Waterworks.

sentences.zh: 榮少與隋文帝親狎，帝嘗與夜坐月下，謂榮曰：「吾仰觀玄象，俯察人事，周曆已盡，我其代之。」

translations.literal: Rong had been close to Emperor Wen of Sui from youth; the emperor once sat with him at night beneath the moon and said to Rong: "I look up and observe the dark signs of heaven, look down and examine human affairs — the Zhou mandate is spent; I shall replace it."
translations.idiomatic: Rong had been close to the future Emperor Wen of Sui since youth; one night the two sat together under the moon, and Yang Jian said to him, "I look up at the signs of heaven and down at the affairs of men — the Zhou dynasty's term is spent, and I shall take its place."

sentences.zh: 榮深自結納。

translations.literal: Rong bound himself closely to him in deepest loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Rong pledged himself to Yang Jian ever more deeply.

sentences.zh: 未幾，周宣崩，文帝總百揆，召榮，撫其背笑曰：「吾言驗未？」

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Xuan of Zhou died; Emperor Wen assumed control of all government, summoned Rong, patted his back and laughed, saying: "Has what I said come true or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Xuan of Zhou died; Yang Jian took control of all government affairs, summoned Rong, clapped him on the back, and laughed, "Has what I said come true?"

sentences.zh: 既拜相府樂曹參軍。

translations.literal: He was then appointed staff officer in the music bureau of the chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed staff officer in the music bureau of the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 俄以本官復領籓部大夫。

translations.literal: Soon, while retaining his original post, he also headed the Bureau of Frontier Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, while retaining that post, he also took charge as Grand Master of the Bureau of Frontier Affairs.

sentences.zh: 文帝受禪，引為內史舍人，以龍潛之舊，進爵蒲城郡公，位上儀同。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen received the abdication, he was brought in as Secretary of the Imperial Secretariat; for their old association from the days before he rose to power, he was advanced to Duke of Pucheng Commandery with the rank of Senior Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, he was brought in as Secretary of the Imperial Secretariat; for their old ties from the days before Yang Jian's rise, he was ennobled as Duke of Pucheng Commandery with the rank of Senior Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 累遷通州刺史。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became Inspector of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Inspector of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，西南夷獠多叛，詔榮領八州諸軍事、行軍總管討平之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Renshou era, many southwestern Yi and Liao peoples rebelled; an edict ordered Rong to take command of military affairs across eight provinces and serve as Campaign Commander-in-Chief to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Renshou era, many southwestern tribal peoples rebelled; Rong was ordered to assume command of military affairs across eight provinces and, as Campaign Commander-in-Chief, suppress the revolt.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，入為武候驃騎大將軍，以嚴正聞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, Rong entered the capital as Grand General of Majestic Cavalry of the Martial Guard and was known for stern integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded, Rong entered the capital as Grand General of Majestic Cavalry of the Martial Guard and was known for stern integrity.

sentences.zh: 後黔字首領田羅駒阻清江作亂，夷陵諸郡人夷多應者，詔榮擊平之。

translations.literal: Later Tian Luoju, chieftain of the Qianzi people, blocked the Qing River and raised rebellion; many tribal people in the Yiling region answered him, and an edict ordered Rong to attack and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tian Luoju, chieftain of the Qianzi people, blocked the Qing River and rebelled; many tribal peoples in the Yiling region joined him, and an edict ordered Rong to attack and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 遷左候衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Garrison Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Garrison Guard General.

sentences.zh: 從帝西征吐谷渾，拜銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor on the western campaign against the Tuyuhun and was granted Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor on the western campaign against the Tuyuhun and was granted Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，以功進左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he was advanced for merit to Left Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign he was advanced for merit to Left Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝復事遼東，榮以為中國疲弊，萬乘不宜屢動，乃言於帝，請止行。

translations.literal: The next year, when the emperor again undertook the Liaodong campaign, Rong considered the realm exhausted and that the sovereign should not move repeatedly; he spoke to the emperor and asked him to halt the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the emperor again undertook the Liaodong campaign, Rong considered the realm exhausted and that the sovereign should not move repeatedly; he spoke to the emperor and asked him to halt the expedition.

sentences.zh: 帝不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept this.

sentences.zh: 復從軍攻遼東城，榮親蒙矢石，晝夜不釋甲胄。

translations.literal: He again followed the army to attack Liaodong city; Rong personally braved arrows and stones and day and night never removed his armor.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the army to attack Liaodong city; Rong personally braved arrows and stones and day and night never removed his armor.

sentences.zh: 帝知之大悅，每勞勉之。

translations.literal: When the emperor learned of this he was greatly pleased and repeatedly praised and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this he was greatly pleased and repeatedly praised and encouraged him.

sentences.zh: 帝后以榮年老，欲出為郡。

translations.literal: Later the emperor, considering Rong's advanced age, wished to send him out to govern a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor, considering Rong's advanced age, wished to send him out to govern a commandery.

sentences.zh: 榮陳請不願。

translations.literal: Rong submitted a petition that he did not wish this.
translations.idiomatic: Rong submitted a petition that he did not wish this.

sentences.zh: 哀之，拜右候衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Taking pity on him, the emperor appointed him Right Garrison Guard Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Taking pity on him, the emperor appointed him Right Garrison Guard Grand General.

sentences.zh: 後數日，帝謂百僚曰：「誠心純至如郭榮者，固無比矣。」

translations.literal: Some days later the emperor told the hundred officials: "For pure and wholehearted devotion like Guo Rong's, there is truly no equal."
translations.idiomatic: Some days later the emperor told the hundred officials, "For pure and wholehearted devotion like Guo Rong's, there is truly no equal."

sentences.zh: 楊玄感之亂，帝令馳守太原。

translations.literal: During Yang Xuangan's rebellion the emperor ordered him to ride swiftly to defend Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: During Yang Xuangan's rebellion the emperor ordered him to ride swiftly to defend Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 明年，從帝至柳城，卒於懷遠鎮。

translations.literal: The next year he followed the emperor to Liucheng and died at Huaiyuan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he followed the emperor to Liucheng and died at Huaiyuan Garrison.

sentences.zh: 帝為廢朝，贈兵部尚書，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: The emperor suspended court for a day and posthumously granted him Minister of War with the posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspended court for a day and posthumously granted him Minister of War with the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 子福善。

translations.literal: His son Fushan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fushan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 龐晃，字元顯，榆林人也。

translations.literal: Pang Huang, courtesy name Yuanxian, was a native of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Huang, courtesy name Yuanxian, was a native of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 父虯，周驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: His father Qiu was General of Agile Cavalry under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qiu had served Zhou as General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 晃少以良家子召補州都督。

translations.literal: In youth Huang was summoned as a respectable-family youth and appointed Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: While still young, Huang was summoned as a youth of good family and appointed Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 周文帝署大都督，領親信兵，常置左右。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou appointed him Grand Commander, placed him in charge of trusted troops, and kept him constantly at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou appointed him Grand Commander, put him in charge of trusted troops, and kept him constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 晃因徙居關中。

translations.literal: Huang thereby moved to live in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Huang moved to Guanzhong as a result.

sentences.zh: 後遷驃騎將軍，襲爵比陽侯。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and inherited the title Marquis of Biyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and inherited the title Marquis of Biyang.

sentences.zh: 衛王直出領襄州，晃以本官從。

translations.literal: When Prince Wei Zhi went out to take charge of Xiangzhou, Huang accompanied him in his existing office.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wei Zhi went out to take charge of Xiangzhou, Huang accompanied him in his existing office.

sentences.zh: 尋與長湖西元定擊江南，孤軍深入，沒于陳。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he joined Yu Yuanding of Changhuxi in an attack on Jiangnan; penetrating deep with an isolated force, he was lost to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he joined Yu Yuanding of Changhuxi in an attack on Jiangnan; advancing deep with an isolated force, he was captured by Chen.

sentences.zh: 數年，衛王直遣晃弟車騎將軍元俊賚絹八百匹贖焉，乃得歸。

translations.literal: After several years, Prince Wei Zhi sent Huang's younger brother, General of Chariots and Cavalry Yuanyu, bearing eight hundred bolts of silk to ransom him, and only then was he able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, Prince Wei Zhi sent Huang's younger brother Yuanyu, General of Chariots and Cavalry, with eight hundred bolts of silk to ransom him, and only then was Huang able to return.

sentences.zh: 拜上儀同，復事衛王。

translations.literal: He was appointed Senior Attendant and again served Prince Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Senior Attendant and again served Prince Wei.

sentences.zh: 時隋文帝出為隨州刺史，路經襄陽，衛王令晃詣文帝。

translations.literal: At that time the future Emperor Wen of Sui had been sent out as Inspector of Suizhou; passing through Xiangyang on the way, Prince Wei ordered Huang to call on him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the future Emperor Wen of Sui had been sent out as Inspector of Suizhou; as he passed through Xiangyang on the way, Prince Wei ordered Huang to call on him.

sentences.zh: 晃知帝非常人，深自結納。

translations.literal: Huang knew that the emperor was no ordinary man and bound himself closely to him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang knew that Yang Jian was no ordinary man and pledged himself to him ever more deeply.

sentences.zh: 及帝去官歸京師，晃迎見於襄邑。

translations.literal: When the emperor resigned his post and returned to the capital, Huang went to meet him at Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian resigned his post and returned to the capital, Huang went to meet him at Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 帝甚歡，與晃同飯，晃因曰：「公相貌非常，名在圖籙，九五之日，幸願不忘。」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and shared a meal with Huang; Huang then said: "Your appearance is extraordinary, your name is in the prophetic books — when the day of the nine-five arrives, I hope you will not forget me."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian was greatly pleased and shared a meal with Huang; Huang then said, "Your appearance is extraordinary, your name is in the prophetic books — when the day of supreme rule arrives, I hope you will not forget me."

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「何妄言也！」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "What wild talk!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian laughed and said, "What wild talk!"

sentences.zh: 頃之，有一雄雉鳴於庭，帝令晃射之，曰：「中則有賞。

translations.literal: Before long a cock pheasant cried in the courtyard; the emperor had Huang shoot at it and said: "If you hit it, there will be a reward.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a cock pheasant cried in the courtyard; Yang Jian had Huang shoot at it and said, "If you hit it, there will be a reward.

sentences.zh: 然富貴之日，持以為驗。」

translations.literal: Yet when the day of wealth and rank comes, hold this as proof."
translations.idiomatic: But when the day of wealth and rank comes, hold this as proof."

sentences.zh: 文帝受禪，與晃言及之，晃再拜曰：「陛下君臨宇內，猶憶曩時之言？」

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen accepted the abdication, he spoke of this with Huang; Huang bowed twice and said: "Your Majesty now rules all within the realm — do you still remember what was said in those days?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen accepted the abdication, he spoke of this with Huang; Huang bowed twice and said, "Your Majesty now rules all within the realm — do you still remember what was said in those days?"

sentences.zh: 上笑曰：「公此言何得忘也！」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "How could I forget words like that!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "How could I forget words like that!"

sentences.zh: 尋加上開府，拜右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was given the rank of Senior Opening Grandee and appointed General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Huang was given the rank of Senior Opening Grandee and appointed General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 進爵為公。

translations.literal: His noble rank was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: His noble rank was advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 河間王弘之擊突厥。

translations.literal: He accompanied Prince Hejian Hong in an attack on the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Prince Hejian of Hejian in an attack on the Turks.

sentences.zh: 晃性剛悍。

translations.literal: Huang was by nature fierce and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was by nature fierce and overbearing.

sentences.zh: 時廣平王雄當途用事，勢傾朝廷，晁每陵侮之。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Guangping Yang Xiong held power on the road to office and his influence overshadowed the court; Chao repeatedly treated him with contempt and insult.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince of Guangping Yang Xiong was in power and his influence eclipsed the court; Huang repeatedly showed him contempt.

sentences.zh: 嘗於軍中臥，見雄不起，雄甚銜之。

translations.literal: Once, lying in camp, he did not rise when he saw Xiong; Xiong deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while lying in camp, he did not rise when he saw Xiong; Xiong deeply resented this.

sentences.zh: 復與高熲有隙。

translations.literal: He also had a rift with Gao Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: He also had a rift with Gao Jiong.

sentences.zh: 二人屢譖晃，由是宿衛十餘年，官不得進。

translations.literal: The two repeatedly slandered Huang, and for this reason he served in palace guard for more than ten years without advancement in rank.
translations.idiomatic: The two repeatedly slandered Huang, and for this reason he served in palace guard for more than ten years without advancement in rank.

sentences.zh: 出為懷州刺史，遷原州總管，卒于官。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Inspector of Huaizhou, transferred to Area Commander of Yuanzhou, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Inspector of Huaizhou, transferred to Area Commander of Yuanzhou, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 帝為廢朝，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: The emperor suspended court in mourning; his posthumous title was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspended court in mourning; his posthumous title was Jing ("Respectful").

sentences.zh: 子長壽，頗知名，位驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: His son Changshou was fairly well known and rose to General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changshou was fairly well known and rose to General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 李安，字玄德，隴西狄道人也。

translations.literal: Li An, courtesy name Xuande, was a native of Didao in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li An, courtesy name Xuande, was a native of Didao in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 父蔚，仕周，為相燕恆三州刺史、襄武縣公。

translations.literal: His father Wei served Zhou as Inspector of Xiang, Yan, and Heng and was Duke of Xiangwu County.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wei had served Zhou as Inspector of Xiang, Yan, and Heng and was Duke of Xiangwu County.

sentences.zh: 安美姿容，善騎射。

translations.literal: An was handsome in appearance and skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: An was handsome in appearance and skilled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 天和中，襲爵襄武公，授儀同、小司右上士。

translations.literal: During the Tianhe era he inherited the title Duke of Xiangwu and was granted the rank of Attendant and Senior Clerk of the Right in the Minor Office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianhe era he inherited the title Duke of Xiangwu and was granted the rank of Attendant and Senior Clerk of the Right in the Minor Office.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝作相，引之左右，遷職方中大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui became Chancellor, he brought An into his entourage and promoted him to Middle Grandee of the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became Chancellor, he brought An into his entourage and promoted him to Middle Grandee of the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 復拜安弟哲為儀同。

translations.literal: He also appointed An's younger brother Zhe as Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He also appointed An's younger brother Zhe as Attendant.

sentences.zh: 安叔父梁州刺史璋時在京師，與周趙王謀害帝，誘哲為內應。

translations.literal: An's uncle Zhang, then Inspector of Liangzhou, was in the capital and plotted with the Zhou Prince of Zhao to harm the emperor, trying to induce Zhe to serve as an inside accomplice.
translations.idiomatic: An's uncle Zhang, then Inspector of Liangzhou, was in the capital and plotted with the Zhou Prince of Zhao to harm Yang Jian, trying to induce Zhe to serve as an inside accomplice.

sentences.zh: 哲謂安曰：「寢之則不忠，言之則不義，失忠與義，何以立身？」

translations.literal: Zhe said to An: "If I conceal it, I am disloyal; if I speak of it, I am unrighteous — losing both loyalty and righteousness, how can I stand as a man?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhe said to An, "If I conceal it, I am disloyal; if I speak of it, I am unrighteous — losing both loyalty and righteousness, how can I stand as a man?"

sentences.zh: 安曰：「丞相，父也，其可背乎！」

translations.literal: An said: "The Chancellor is like a father — how could I betray him!"
translations.idiomatic: An said, "The Chancellor is like a father — how could I betray him!"

sentences.zh: 遂陰白之。

translations.literal: He then secretly reported it.
translations.idiomatic: He then secretly reported the plot.

sentences.zh: 及趙王等伏誅，將加官賞，安頓首曰：「豈可將叔父之命以求官賞？」

translations.literal: When the Prince of Zhao and the others were executed, as rewards and promotions were about to be granted, An prostrated himself and said: "How could I use my uncle's life to seek rank and reward?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Zhao and the others were executed, as rewards and promotions were about to be granted, An prostrated himself and said, "How could I use my uncle's life to seek rank and reward?"

sentences.zh: 於是俯伏流涕，悲不自勝。

translations.literal: He then lay prostrate weeping, overcome with grief beyond his own bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He then lay prostrate weeping, overcome with grief he could not contain.

sentences.zh: 帝為之改容曰：「我為汝特存璋子。」

translations.literal: The emperor's expression changed and he said: "For your sake I have specially spared Zhang's son."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's expression changed and he said, "For your sake I have specially spared Zhang's son."

sentences.zh: 乃命有司罪止璋身，帝亦為安隱其事而不言。

translations.literal: He then ordered the authorities to limit punishment to Zhang himself, and for An's sake he also concealed the matter and did not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the authorities to limit punishment to Zhang himself, and for An's sake he also concealed the matter and did not speak of it.

sentences.zh: 尋授安開府，進封趙郡公，哲上儀同、黃台縣男。

translations.literal: Soon afterward An was granted the rank of Opening Grandee and advanced to Duke of Zhao commandery; Zhe was made Senior Attendant and Baron of Huangtai County.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward An was granted the rank of Opening Grandee and advanced to Duke of Zhao commandery; Zhe was made Senior Attendant and Baron of Huangtai County.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，歷內史侍郎、尚書左丞、黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded, An successively served as Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Left Assistant Director in the Ministry of State Affairs, and Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, An successively served as Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Left Assistant Director in the Ministry of State Affairs, and Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役為楊素司馬，仍領行軍總管，率蜀兵順流東下。

translations.literal: During the campaign to pacify Chen he served as chief of staff to Yang Su while also commanding the campaign army, leading Shu troops downstream to the east.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign to pacify Chen he served as chief of staff to Yang Su while also commanding the campaign army, leading Shu troops downstream to the east.

sentences.zh: 時陳人屯白沙，安謂諸將曰：「水戰非北人所長。

translations.literal: When the Chen forces were encamped at Baisha, An told the generals: "Naval combat is not what northerners excel at.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen forces were encamped at Baisha, An told the generals, "Naval combat is not what northerners excel at.

sentences.zh: 今陳人依險泊船，必輕我無備。

translations.literal: Now the Chen men have moored their boats in a defensible position; they are sure to think us unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Chen men have moored their boats in a defensible position; they are sure to think us unprepared.

sentences.zh: 夜襲之，賊可破也。」

translations.literal: A night attack can break them."
translations.idiomatic: A night attack can break them."

sentences.zh: 安率眾先鋒，大破陳師。

translations.literal: An led the vanguard and greatly defeated the Chen army.
translations.idiomatic: An led the vanguard and greatly defeated the Chen army.

sentences.zh: 詔書勞勉，進位上大將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict praised and comforted him; he was advanced to Senior Grand General and Inspector of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised and comforted him; he was advanced to Senior Grand General and Inspector of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 轉鄧州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of Deng Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Inspector of Deng Province.

sentences.zh: 求為內職，帝重違其意，除左領左右將軍。

translations.literal: He requested an inner-court post; the emperor, reluctant to refuse him, appointed him Left Commander of the Left and Right Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He requested an inner-court post; the emperor, reluctant to refuse him, appointed him Left Commander of the Left and Right Guards.

sentences.zh: 遷右領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 拜哲開府儀同三司、備身將軍。

translations.literal: Zhe was made Opening Grandee with the Honored Title Equal to the Three Dukes and General of the Personal Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe was made Opening Grandee with the Honored Title Equal to the Three Dukes and General of the Personal Guard.

sentences.zh: 兄弟俱典禁衛，恩信甚重。

translations.literal: The brothers both held posts in the palace guard, and the emperor's favor and trust in them were very great.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers both held posts in the palace guard, and the emperor's favor and trust in them were very great.

sentences.zh: 十八年，突厥犯塞，以安為行軍總管，從楊素擊之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, when the Turks raided the frontier, An was made Campaign Commander-in-Chief and joined Yang Su in attacking them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, when the Turks raided the frontier, An was made Campaign Commander-in-Chief and joined Yang Su in attacking them.

sentences.zh: 安別出長川，會虜渡河，與戰破之。

translations.literal: An took a separate route out through Changchuan, encountered the enemy crossing the river, fought them, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: An took a separate route out through Changchuan, encountered the enemy crossing the river, fought them, and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 仁壽元年，出安為甯州刺史，哲為衛州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Renshou, An was sent out as Inspector of Ningzhou and Zhe as Inspector of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Renshou, An was sent out as Inspector of Ningzhou and Zhe as Inspector of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 安子瓊，哲子瑋，始自繈褓，乳養宮中，至是年八九歲，始命歸家。

translations.literal: An's son Qiong and Zhe's son Wei, from infancy had been nursed and raised in the palace; by this time they were eight or nine years old and were at last ordered to return home.
translations.idiomatic: An's son Qiong and Zhe's son Wei had been nursed and raised in the palace from infancy; by this time they were eight or nine years old and were at last ordered to return home.

sentences.zh: 其親顧如是。

translations.literal: Their kinship and solicitude were such.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's affectionate concern for their families extended even this far.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗言及作相時事，因湣安兄弟滅親奉國，乃下詔曰：「先王立教，以義斷恩，割親愛之情，盡事君之道，用能弘獎大節，體此至公。

translations.literal: The emperor once spoke of events when he had been Chancellor; moved to pity that the An brothers had set aside kinship to serve the state, he issued an edict saying: "The ancient kings established teaching to sever affection by righteousness, cut through the bonds of cherished kin, and fulfill the way of serving one's lord — thereby able to magnify and reward great integrity and embody this supreme fairness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once spoke of events from when he had been Chancellor; moved to pity that the An brothers had set aside kinship to serve the state, he issued an edict saying, "The ancient kings established teaching to sever affection by righteousness, cut through the bonds of cherished kin, and fulfill the way of serving one's lord — thereby able to magnify and reward great integrity and embody this supreme fairness.

sentences.zh: 往者朕登庸惟始，王業初基，甯州刺史趙郡公李安，其叔璋潛結籓枝，包藏不逞。

translations.literal: In the past, when I first took office and the royal enterprise was just being founded, Li An, Duke of Zhao commandery and Inspector of Ningzhou — his uncle Zhang secretly allied with princely branches and harbored rebellious designs.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, when I first took office and the royal enterprise was just being founded, Li An, Duke of Zhao commandery and Inspector of Ningzhou — his uncle Zhang secretly allied with princely branches and harbored rebellious designs.

sentences.zh: 安與弟哲深知逆順，披露丹心，凶謀既彰，罪人斯得。

translations.literal: An and his brother Zhe deeply understood treason and loyalty and laid bare their loyal hearts; once the wicked plot was exposed, the guilty were seized.
translations.idiomatic: An and his brother Zhe deeply understood treason and loyalty and laid bare their loyal hearts; once the wicked plot was exposed, the guilty were seized.

sentences.zh: 朕每念誠節，嘉之無已。

translations.literal: Whenever I think of their sincere integrity, my praise knows no end.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I think of their sincere integrity, my praise knows no end.

sentences.zh: 但以事涉其親，猶有疑惑，欲使安等名教之方，自處有地。

translations.literal: But because the affair involved their kin, I still had doubts, wishing to enable An and the others to have proper standing within the norms of name and teaching.
translations.idiomatic: But because the affair involved their kin, I still had doubts, wishing to enable An and the others to have proper standing within the norms of name and teaching.

sentences.zh: 朕常為思審，遂致淹年。

translations.literal: I often pondered the matter carefully, and so years passed.
translations.idiomatic: I often pondered the matter carefully, and so years passed.

sentences.zh: 今更詳案聖典，求諸往事，父子天性，忠孝猶不並立，況復叔侄恩輕，情禮本有差降。

translations.literal: Now examining the sacred canon more closely and seeking guidance in past events — the nature of father and son, yet loyalty and filial piety still cannot both stand; how much more so uncle and nephew, where affection is lighter and sentiment and ritual naturally have gradations.
translations.idiomatic: Now examining the sacred canon more closely and seeking guidance in past events — even between father and son, whose bond is innate, loyalty and filial piety still cannot both stand; how much more so between uncle and nephew, where affection is lighter and sentiment and ritual naturally have gradations.

sentences.zh: 忘私奉國，深得正理。

translations.literal: To forget private ties and serve the state — this deeply accords with correct principle.
translations.idiomatic: To forget private ties and serve the state — this deeply accords with correct principle.

sentences.zh: 宜錄舊勳，重弘賞命。」

translations.literal: Their former merit should be recorded and rewards and commands magnified anew."
translations.idiomatic: Their former merit should be recorded and rewards and commands magnified anew."

sentences.zh: 於是拜安、哲俱為柱國，賜縑各五十匹、馬百匹、羊千口。

translations.literal: Thereupon both An and Zhe were appointed Pillars of the State, and each was granted fifty bolts of silk, a hundred horses, and a thousand sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon both An and Zhe were appointed Pillars of the State, and each was granted fifty bolts of silk, a hundred horses, and a thousand sheep.

sentences.zh: 以哲為備身將軍。

translations.literal: Zhe was made Personal Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe was made Personal Guard General.

sentences.zh: 進封順陽郡公。

translations.literal: His noble rank was advanced to Duke of Shunyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Duke of Shunyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 安謂親族曰：「雖家獲全，而叔父遭禍，今奉此詔，悲愧交懷。」

translations.literal: An said to his kin: "Though our family has been preserved whole, my uncle met with disaster; receiving this edict now, grief and shame fill my heart together."
translations.idiomatic: An said to his kin, "Though our family has been preserved whole, my uncle met with disaster; receiving this edict now, grief and shame fill my heart together."

sentences.zh: 因歔欷悲感，不能自勝。

translations.literal: He then sobbed in grief, unable to contain himself.
translations.idiomatic: He then sobbed in grief, unable to contain himself.

sentences.zh: 先患水病，於是疾甚而卒。

translations.literal: He had long suffered from edema; at this his illness grew severe and he died.
translations.idiomatic: He had long suffered from edema; at this his illness grew severe and he died.

sentences.zh: 諡曰懷。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Huai.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Huai ("Cherishing").

sentences.zh: 子瓊嗣。

translations.literal: His son Qiong succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 少子孝恭，最知名。

translations.literal: His youngest son Xiaogong was the best known.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Xiaogong was the best known.

sentences.zh: 哲，煬帝時工部尚書，後坐事除名，配防嶺南，道卒。

translations.literal: Zhe, during Emperor Yang's reign, was Minister of Works; later he was stripped of rank for an offense, assigned to guard duty in Lingnan, and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe, during Emperor Yang's reign, was Minister of Works; later he was stripped of rank for an offense, assigned to guard duty in Lingnan, and died on the road.

sentences.zh: 楊尚希

translations.literal: Yang Shangxi
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shangxi

sentences.zh: 楊尚希，弘農人也。

translations.literal: Yang Shangxi was a native of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shangxi was a native of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 祖真，魏天水太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen was Administrator of Tianshui under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen had served Wei as Administrator of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 父承寶，商直淅三州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Chengbao was Inspector of Shang, Zhi, and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengbao had served as Inspector of Shang, Zhi, and Xi.

sentences.zh: 尚希齠齔而孤，年十一，辭母請受業長安。

translations.literal: Shangxi lost his father while still in infancy; at eleven he took leave of his mother and asked to study in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Shangxi lost his father while still in infancy; at eleven he took leave of his mother and asked to study in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 范陽盧辯見而異之，令入太學，專精不倦，同輩皆共推服。

translations.literal: Lu Bian of Fanyang saw him and considered him extraordinary, had him enter the Imperial Academy; he applied himself without weariness, and his fellows all respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bian of Fanyang saw him and considered him extraordinary, had him enter the Imperial Academy, and he applied himself without weariness until all his fellows respected him.

sentences.zh: 周文帝嘗親臨釋奠，尚希時年十八，令講《孝經》，詞旨可觀。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou once personally attended the sacrificial ceremony; Shangxi was then eighteen and was ordered to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety — his words and meaning were worthy of note.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou once personally attended the sacrificial ceremony; Shangxi was then eighteen and was ordered to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety — his words and meaning were worthy of note.

sentences.zh: 文帝奇之，賜姓普六茹氏。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at him and granted him the surname Puliuru.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled at him and granted him the surname Puliuru.

sentences.zh: 擢為國子博士，累轉舍人上士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Academician of the Imperial University and rose in succession to Senior Clerk of Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Academician of the Imperial University and rose in succession to Senior Clerk of Attendants.

sentences.zh: 明、武世，曆太學博士、太子宮尹、計部中大夫。

translations.literal: During the Ming and Wu reigns he served successively as Academician of the Imperial University, Steward of the Heir Apparent's Palace, and Middle Grandee of the Accounts Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: During the Ming and Wu reigns he served successively as Academician of the Imperial University, Steward of the Heir Apparent's Palace, and Middle Grandee of the Accounts Bureau.

sentences.zh: 賜爵高都侯，東京司憲中大夫。

translations.literal: He was granted the title Marquis of Gaodu and made Middle Grandee of the Eastern Capital Judicial Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the title Marquis of Gaodu and made Middle Grandee of the Eastern Capital Judicial Bureau.

sentences.zh: 撫慰山東、河北，至相州而宣帝崩，與相州總管尉遲迥發喪于館。

translations.literal: While pacifying and comforting Shandong and Hebei, he reached Xiangzhou when Emperor Xuan died; together with Yuchi Jiong, Area Commander of Xiangzhou, he announced the mourning at the official residence.
translations.idiomatic: While pacifying and comforting Shandong and Hebei, he reached Xiangzhou when Emperor Xuan died; together with Yuchi Jiong, Area Commander of Xiangzhou, he announced the mourning at the official residence.

sentences.zh: 尚希出謂左右曰：「蜀公哭不哀而視不安，將有他計。

translations.literal: Shangxi went out and said to those around him: "The Duke of Shu weeps without grief and his gaze is unsettled — he must have another plan in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Shangxi went out and said to those around him, "The Duke of Shu weeps without grief and his gaze is unsettled — he must have another plan in mind.

sentences.zh: 吾不去，將及於難。」

translations.literal: If I do not leave, I shall be caught up in disaster."
translations.idiomatic: If I do not leave, I shall be caught up in disaster."

sentences.zh: 遂夜遁。

translations.literal: He fled that night.
translations.idiomatic: He fled that night.

sentences.zh: 及明，迥方覺，令數十騎追不及，遂歸京師。

translations.literal: When dawn came Jiong realized it only then and sent several dozen horsemen in pursuit but could not overtake him; Shangxi returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When dawn came Jiong realized it only then and sent several dozen horsemen in pursuit but could not overtake him; Shangxi returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝以尚希宗室之望，又背迥而至，待之甚厚。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui, because Shangxi enjoyed standing among the imperial clan and had abandoned Jiong to come to him, treated him with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui, because Shangxi enjoyed standing among the imperial clan and had abandoned Jiong to come to him, treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 及迥屯兵武陟，遣尚希領宗室兵三千人鎮潼關。

translations.literal: When Jiong stationed troops at Wuzhi, Emperor Wen sent Shangxi to lead three thousand clan troops to guard Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiong stationed troops at Wuzhi, Emperor Wen sent Shangxi to lead three thousand clan troops to guard Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 尋授司會中大夫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Middle Grandee of the Bureau of Accounting.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Middle Grandee of the Bureau of Accounting.

sentences.zh: 文帝受禪，拜度支尚書，進爵為公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen accepted the abdication, Shangxi was appointed Minister of Revenue and his noble rank was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen accepted the abdication, Shangxi was appointed Minister of Revenue and his noble rank was advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，出為河南道行台兵部尚書，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was sent out as Minister of War for the Henan Circuit Office and given the Grand Master with the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was sent out as Minister of War for the Henan Circuit Office and given the Grand Master with the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 尚希時見天下州郡過多，上表以為「今郡縣倍多於古，或地無百里，數縣並置，或戶不滿千，二郡分領。

translations.literal: Shangxi then saw that prefectures and commanderies throughout the realm were too numerous and submitted a memorial stating: "Today commanderies and counties are more than twice as many as in antiquity — sometimes over a territory of less than a hundred li several counties are established side by side, or over households numbering fewer than a thousand two commanderies divide the oversight.
translations.idiomatic: Shangxi then saw that prefectures and commanderies throughout the realm were too numerous and submitted a memorial stating, "Today commanderies and counties are more than twice as many as in antiquity — sometimes over a territory of less than a hundred li several counties are established side by side, or over households numbering fewer than a thousand two commanderies divide the oversight.

sentences.zh: 具僚以眾，資費日多，吏卒又倍，租調歲減。

translations.literal: Staff assistants grow ever more numerous, expenditures daily increase, clerks and soldiers again double, and land tax and corvée levies diminish year by year.
translations.idiomatic: Staff assistants grow ever more numerous, expenditures daily increase, clerks and soldiers again double, and land tax and corvée levies diminish year by year.

sentences.zh: 清幹良材，百分無一，動須數萬，如何可充！

translations.literal: Capable and upright talent — not one in a hundred; yet tens of thousands are needed at every turn — how can this be supplied!
translations.idiomatic: Capable and upright talent — not one in a hundred; yet tens of thousands are needed at every turn — how can this be supplied!

sentences.zh: 所謂人少官多，十羊九牧。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by too few people and too many officials — ten sheep and nine shepherds.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by too few people and too many officials — ten sheep and nine shepherds.

sentences.zh: 今存要去閑，並小為大，國家則不虧粟帛，選用則易得賢才。」

translations.literal: Now if we keep what is essential, remove what is idle, and merge small units into large ones, the state will not lose grain and silk, and in selection and appointment worthy talent will be easy to obtain."
translations.idiomatic: Now if we keep what is essential, remove what is idle, and merge small units into large ones, the state will not lose grain and silk, and in selection and appointment worthy talent will be easy to obtain."

sentences.zh: 帝覽而嘉之，遂罷天下諸郡。

translations.literal: The emperor read it and praised it, and thereupon abolished all commanderies throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and praised it, and thereupon abolished all commanderies throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 後歷位瀛州刺史、兵部、禮部二尚書，授上儀同。

translations.literal: Later he served successively as Inspector of Yingzhou and as Minister of War and Minister of Rites, and was granted the rank of Senior Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served successively as Inspector of Yingzhou and as Minister of War and Minister of Rites, and was granted the rank of Senior Attendant.

sentences.zh: 尚希性惇厚，兼以學業自通，甚有雅望，為朝廷所重。

translations.literal: Shangxi was by nature sincere and generous; he had also mastered learning on his own and enjoyed great refined standing, and the court held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Shangxi was by nature sincere and generous; he had also mastered learning on his own and enjoyed great refined standing, and the court held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 上時每旦臨朝，日側不倦，尚希諫以為「陛下宜舉大綱，責成宰輔。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor every morning attended court, tireless until the sun slanted westward; Shangxi remonstrated, saying, "Your Majesty should grasp the great principles and hold the chief ministers accountable.
translations.idiomatic: In those days the emperor held court every morning and never flagged, even when the sun was westering. Shangxi remonstrated with him: "Your Majesty should grasp the great principles and hold your chief ministers accountable.

sentences.zh: 繁碎之務，非人主所宜親。」

translations.literal: Petty, piecemeal business is not what the human sovereign should personally attend to."
translations.idiomatic: Petty, piecemeal business is not work the sovereign himself should take in hand."

sentences.zh: 上歡然曰：「公愛我者。」

translations.literal: The emperor said with pleasure, "You truly care for me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, pleased, "You truly care for me."

sentences.zh: 尚稀有足疾，謂曰：「蒲州出美酒，足堪養病，屈公臥臨之。」

translations.literal: Shangxi had an ailment of the foot, and the emperor said to him, "Puzhou produces fine wine, quite enough to nurse an illness — I beg you to go lie there and govern from your couch."
translations.idiomatic: Shangxi was troubled by a foot ailment, and the emperor told him, "Puzhou produces fine wine, enough to nurse you back to health — I must ask you to go lie there and govern the prefecture from your couch."

sentences.zh: 於是拜蒲州刺史，仍領本州宗團驃騎。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed Inspector of Puzhou, while continuing to hold the post of regional militia Biaoqi commander for the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was appointed Inspector of Puzhou, while continuing to command the prefecture's regional militia cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尚希在州，甚有惠政，復引瀵水立堤防，開稻田數千頃，人賴其利。

translations.literal: Shangxi in the prefecture had very benevolent administration; he again led in the Fen River, built dikes and embankments, and opened several thousand qing of rice fields — the people relied on the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: As inspector, Shangxi governed with great benevolence. He diverted the Fen River, built dikes and embankments, and opened several thousand qing of rice paddies; the people prospered from his work.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 諡曰平。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Ping.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Ping ("Balanced").

sentences.zh: 子旻嗣，後封丹水縣公，位安定郡丞。

translations.literal: His son Min succeeded him; later he was enfeoffed as Duke of Danshui County and held the post of Assistant Administrator of Anding commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Min succeeded him and was later enfeoffed as Duke of Danshui County and appointed Assistant Administrator of Anding commandery.

sentences.zh: 張煚，字士鴻，河間鄚人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiong, courtesy name Shihong, was a man of Mo in Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiong, whose courtesy name was Shihong, came from Mo in Hejian commandery.

sentences.zh: 父羨，少好學，多所通涉，仕魏，為蕩難將軍。

translations.literal: His father Xian, from youth fond of learning, broadly mastered many subjects; he served Wei and was General Who Pacifies Difficulties.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xian loved learning from youth and mastered many fields of study. Under Wei he served as General Who Pacifies Difficulties.

sentences.zh: 從武帝入關，累遷銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Wu in entering the Pass and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master with the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wu of Zhou when the army entered the Pass and rose through successive posts to Grand Master with the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 周文引為從事中郎，賜姓叱羅氏。

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Zhou brought him in as Attendant Gentleman and bestowed on him the surname Chiluo.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen of Zhou brought him into service as Attendant Gentleman and granted him the surname Chiluo.

sentences.zh: 曆司織大夫、雍州中從事、應州刺史、儀同三司，賜爵虞鄉縣公。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Grand Master of Weaving, Middle Attendant of Yongzhou, Inspector of Yingzhou, and Attendant Equal to the Three Dukes, and was granted the title Duke of Yuxiang County.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Grand Master of Weaving, Middle Attendant of Yongzhou, Inspector of Yingzhou, and Attendant Equal to the Three Dukes, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yuxiang County.

sentences.zh: 復入為司成中大夫，典國史。

translations.literal: He again entered service as Grand Master Director of Education and managed the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Grand Master Director of Education and was put in charge of the national history.

sentences.zh: 周代公卿，類多武將，唯羨以素業自通，甚為當時所重。

translations.literal: In the Zhou dynasty the high ministers were mostly military generals; only Xian, through plain scholarly accomplishment, made his own way and was greatly esteemed by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou, high ministers were mostly military men; Xian alone rose through scholarly accomplishment and was greatly esteemed in his day.

sentences.zh: 後以年老致仕。

translations.literal: Later, on account of old age, he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he retired from office on account of his age.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，欽其德望，以書征之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he admired Xian's virtue and standing and summoned him by letter.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, he admired Xian's virtue and reputation and summoned him by letter.

sentences.zh: 及謁見，敕令勿拜，扶杖升殿，上降榻執手，與之同坐，宴語久之，賜以几杖。

translations.literal: When he came to audience, an edict ordered that he not bow; supported by his staff he ascended the hall, the emperor came down from the couch, took his hand, and sat with him together; they feasted and talked for a long time, and he was granted a armrest and staff.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to audience, the emperor ordered that he not bow. Leaning on his staff, Xian ascended the hall; the emperor came down from his couch, took his hand, and sat with him as an equal. They talked at leisure for a long time, and the emperor granted him an armrest and walking staff.

sentences.zh: 會遷都龍首，羨上表勸以儉約，上優詔答之。

translations.literal: When the capital was moved to Longshou, Xian submitted a memorial urging thrift, and the emperor answered with a gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved the capital to Longshou, Xian submitted a memorial urging frugality, and the emperor replied with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈滄州刺史，諡曰定。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously made Inspector of Cangzhou; his posthumous title was Ding.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made Inspector of Cangzhou and given the posthumous title Ding ("Settled").

sentences.zh: 所撰《老子》、《莊子》義，名《道言》，五十二篇。

translations.literal: What he wrote — commentaries on the Laozi and Zhuangzi — was titled Dao Discourse, in fifty-two chapters.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote commentaries on the Laozi and Zhuangzi under the title Dao Discourse, in fifty-two chapters.

sentences.zh: 煚好學，有父風。

translations.literal: Jiong loved learning and had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong loved learning and took after his father.

sentences.zh: 仕魏，位員外侍郎。

translations.literal: He served Wei and held the post of Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei he served as Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant.

sentences.zh: 周文引為外兵曹。

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Zhou brought him in as Clerk in the External Military Section.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen of Zhou brought him into service as Clerk in the External Military Section.

sentences.zh: 明、武世，位塚宰司錄，賜爵北平縣子。

translations.literal: In the reigns of Ming and Wu he held the post of Chief Recorder to the Chancellor and was granted the title Viscount of Beiping County.
translations.idiomatic: During the reigns of Emperors Ming and Wu he served as Chief Recorder to the Chancellor and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Beiping County.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，加儀同，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuan he was given the rank of Attendant Equal and advanced in noble rank to baron.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan he was granted the rank of Attendant Equal and ennobled as a baron.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，煚深自推結。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chancellor, Jiong deeply pledged himself in friendship.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was still chancellor, Jiong pledged himself to him in close friendship.

sentences.zh: 帝以其有幹用，甚親遇之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because he had practical capacity, treated him with great intimacy and favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued his practical ability and treated him with great intimacy.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，拜為尚書右丞，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: When the abdication was received, he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and advanced in noble rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne, Jiong was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and ennobled as a marquis.

sentences.zh: 遷太府少卿，領營新都監丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Junior Minister of the Imperial Storehouse and concurrently served as Supervisor of the Directorate for Building the New Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Junior Minister of the Imperial Storehouse and put in charge of supervising construction of the new capital.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂去職，柴毀骨立。

translations.literal: On his father's mourning he left office; his grief consumed him until only skin and bone remained.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father and grieved until he was skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 未期，授儀同三司，襲爵虞鄉縣公。

translations.literal: Before the mourning term was complete, he was granted Attendant Equal to the Three Dukes and inherited the title Duke of Yuxiang County.
translations.idiomatic: Before the mourning period was complete, he was granted the rank of Attendant Equal to the Three Dukes and inherited his father's title as Duke of Yuxiang County.

sentences.zh: 曆太府卿、戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Minister of the Imperial Storehouse and Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Minister of the Imperial Storehouse and Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣為揚州總管，授煚司馬，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, was Regional Commander of Yangzhou, Jiong was appointed his Military Assistant and given the rank of Grand Master with the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, became Regional Commander of Yangzhou, Jiong was appointed his military assistant and granted the rank of Grand Master with the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 煚性和厚有識度，甚有當時譽。

translations.literal: Jiong's nature was generous and substantial, with judgment and breadth of view, and he enjoyed great reputation in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was generous and steady by nature, possessed of judgment and breadth of view, and enjoyed great renown in his day.

sentences.zh: 後拜冀州刺史，晉王廣頻表請之，復為晉王長史，檢校蔣州事。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Inspector of Jizhou; the Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, repeatedly memorialized requesting him, and he again became Chief Secretary to the Prince of Jin and supervised affairs of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Inspector of Jizhou. The Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, repeatedly memorialized asking for him back, and Jiong again became the prince's chief secretary with supervisory authority over Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及晉王為皇太子，復為冀州刺史，位上開府，吏人悅服，稱為良二千石。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin became crown prince, Jiong again became Inspector of Jizhou, holding the rank of Senior Office Opener; officials and people were pleased and submitted, and he was called an excellent two-thousand-shi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin became crown prince, Jiong again served as Inspector of Jizhou with the rank of Senior Office Opener. Officials and common people alike were pleased and submitted to him, and he was hailed as an excellent prefectural governor.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子慧寶，官至絳郡丞。

translations.literal: His son Huibao rose in office to Assistant Administrator of Jiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huibao rose to the post of Assistant Administrator of Jiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，有劉仁恩者，政績為天下第一，擢拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era there was a Liu Ren'en whose administrative achievements ranked first in the realm; he was promoted and appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era there was a Liu Ren'en whose administrative record ranked first in the realm; he was promoted to Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 以行軍總管從楊素伐陳，與素破陳將呂仲肅于荊門，仁恩計功居多，授上大將軍，甚有當時譽。

translations.literal: As campaigning commander he followed Yang Su in attacking Chen; with Su he defeated the Chen general Lü Zhongsu at Jingmen; Ren'en's share in the merit was the greater part, and he was granted Senior General — he enjoyed great reputation in his time.
translations.idiomatic: As campaigning commander he followed Yang Su in the campaign against Chen. With Su he defeated the Chen general Lü Zhongsu at Jingmen, and Ren'en's share of the credit was the greatest; he was granted the rank of Senior General and enjoyed great renown in his day.

sentences.zh: 馮翊郭均、上党馮世期並明悟有幹略，相繼為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Guo Jun of Fengyi and Feng Shiqi of Shangdang were both clear-minded and possessed of practical strategy, and served in succession as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jun of Fengyi and Feng Shiqi of Shangdang were both clear-minded men of practical strategy who served in succession as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 此三人俱顯名於世，然事行闕落，史莫能知。

translations.literal: These three men all won fame in the world, yet their deeds and conduct are lost and incomplete, and the historians cannot know them.
translations.idiomatic: These three men all won fame in the world, yet their deeds have been lost and the historians can no longer recover them.

sentences.zh: 蘇孝慈

translations.literal: Su Xiaoci
translations.idiomatic: Su Xiaoci

sentences.zh: 蘇孝慈，扶風人也。

translations.literal: Su Xiaoci was a man of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Su Xiaoci was a native of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 父武，周兗州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Wu was Inspector of Yanzhou under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wu had served as Inspector of Yanzhou under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 孝慈少沉謹，有器幹，美容儀。

translations.literal: Xiaoci from youth was grave and careful, possessed of capacity and backbone, and handsome in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Xiaoci was grave and careful, possessed of real capacity, and handsome in bearing.

sentences.zh: 仕周，位至工部中大夫，封臨水縣公。

translations.literal: He served Zhou and rose to Grand Master in the Ministry of Works, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Linshui County.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he rose to Grand Master in the Ministry of Works and was enfeoffed as Duke of Linshui County.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，進爵安平郡公，拜太府卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, Xiaoci's noble rank was advanced to Duke of Anping commandery and he was appointed Minister of the Imperial Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, Xiaoci was advanced to Duke of Anping commandery and appointed Minister of the Imperial Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 于時王業初基，征天下匠，纖微之巧，無不畢集。

translations.literal: At that time the royal enterprise had just been founded; craftsmen were summoned from throughout the realm, and the most minute refinements of skill were all gathered together.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the new dynasty was just being established; craftsmen were summoned from throughout the realm, and every refinement of skill was gathered at court.

sentences.zh: 孝慈總其事，世以為能。

translations.literal: Xiaoci oversaw the whole affair, and the age considered him capable.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoci oversaw the whole undertaking, and the world judged him capable.

sentences.zh: 歷位兵部尚書，待遇愈密。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Minister of War, and his treatment grew ever more intimate.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Minister of War, and the emperor's favor toward him grew ever closer.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子勇頗知時政，上欲重宮官之望，多令大臣領其職，拜孝慈太子右衛率，尚書如故。

translations.literal: At that time Crown Prince Yong understood current affairs rather well; the emperor wished to increase the standing of palace officials and often had great ministers hold their posts; Xiaoci was appointed Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, while retaining his post as minister.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Crown Prince Yong took a lively interest in affairs of state. The emperor wished to raise the standing of palace officials and often had great ministers hold their posts; Xiaoci was appointed Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard while retaining his ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 及于陝州置常平倉，轉輸京下，以渭水多沙，乍深乍淺，乃決渭水為渠以屬河，令孝慈督其役，渠成，上善之，又領太子左衛率，仍判工部、戶部二尚書，稱為幹理。

translations.literal: When the Ever-Normal Granary was established at Shazhou to transport grain to the capital, because the Wei River had much sand and was now deep, now shallow, they cut a canal from the Wei to join the Yellow River and had Xiaoci supervise the labor; when the canal was completed the emperor praised it; he also held the post of Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard and concurrently adjudicated the two ministries of Works and Revenue, and was called capable in administration.
translations.idiomatic: When an Ever-Normal Granary was established at Shazhou to supply the capital, the Wei River proved too sandy and treacherously shallow. A canal was cut from the Wei to join the Yellow River, and Xiaoci was put in charge of the work. When the canal was finished the emperor praised it. Xiaoci also served as Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard while concurrently overseeing the Ministries of Works and Revenue, and was acclaimed as an able administrator.

sentences.zh: 進位大將軍，轉工部尚書，率如故。
