translations.literal: He was advanced to General and transferred to Minister of Works; his commandant's post remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General and transferred to Minister of Works, while retaining his post as commandant.

sentences.zh: 先是，以百僚供費不足，台省府寺咸置廨錢，收息取給。

translations.literal: Previously, because the supply expenses of the hundred officials were insufficient, the departments, ministries, and directorates all established office operating funds and drew support from collected interest.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, because official salaries and expenses were insufficient, every department, ministry, and directorate had set up office operating funds and lived off the interest.

sentences.zh: 孝慈以為官與百姓爭利，非興化之道，表請公卿已下給職田各有差，上並納焉。

translations.literal: Xiaoci considered that officials contending with the people for profit was not the way to promote transformation through teaching; he submitted a memorial requesting that from the rank of duke and minister downward salary fields be granted in graded amounts, and the emperor accepted it all.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoci held that for officials to compete with the people for profit was no way to cultivate the realm. He submitted a memorial proposing that officials from the rank of duke and minister downward be granted salary fields in graded amounts, and the emperor accepted the proposal in full.

sentences.zh: 及將廢太子，憚其在東宮，出為淅州刺史。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was about to be deposed, the emperor feared Xiaoci's presence in the Eastern Palace and sent him out as Inspector of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to depose the crown prince, he feared Xiaoci's influence in the Eastern Palace and posted him out as Inspector of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 太子以孝慈去，形於言色。

translations.literal: The crown prince, because Xiaoci was leaving, showed it in word and countenance.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's distress at Xiaoci's departure showed plainly in his words and face.

sentences.zh: 遷洪州總管，俱有惠政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regional Commander of Hongzhou; in both posts he had benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Regional Commander of Hongzhou; in both posts he governed with benevolence.

sentences.zh: 後桂林山越相聚為亂，詔孝慈為行軍總管，擊平之。

translations.literal: Later the Yue of Guilin Mountain gathered together in rebellion; an edict made Xiaoci campaigning commander, and he attacked and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Yue tribes of the Guilin mountains rose in rebellion; Xiaoci was ordered out as campaigning commander and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子會昌。

translations.literal: His son was Huichang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Huichang.

sentences.zh: 孝慈兄順，周眉州刺史。

translations.literal: Xiaoci's elder brother Shun was Inspector of Meizhou under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoci's elder brother Shun had served as Inspector of Meizhou under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 子沙羅，字子粹。

translations.literal: His son Shaluo, courtesy name Zicui.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shaluo, whose courtesy name was Zicui.

sentences.zh: 仕周，以破尉遲迥功，授開府儀同三司，封通泰縣公。

translations.literal: He served Zhou; for merit in defeating Yuwen Jiong he was granted Grand Master Opening the Office Equal to the Three Dukes and enfeoffed as Duke of Tongtai County.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he was granted Grand Master Opening the Office Equal to the Three Dukes and enfeoffed as Duke of Tongtai County for his merit in defeating Yuwen Jiong.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，歷位資、邛二州刺史，檢校利州總管。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era he served in succession as Inspector of Zi and Qiong prefectures and supervised the Regional Commander of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era he served in succession as Inspector of Zi and Qiong prefectures and held supervisory authority over the Regional Commander of Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 從史萬歲擊西爨，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: He followed Shi Wansui in attacking the Western Cuan and was advanced to General.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shi Wansui in the campaign against the Western Cuan and was promoted to General.

sentences.zh: 尋檢校益州總管長史。

translations.literal: Soon he supervised the Chief Secretary to the Regional Commander of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given supervisory authority as Chief Secretary to the Regional Commander of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 及蜀王秀廢，沙羅坐除名。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Shu, Xiu, was deposed, Shaluo was implicated and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiu of Shu was deposed, Shaluo was implicated and stripped of his name and rank.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 子康嗣。

translations.literal: His son Kang succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 元壽，字長壽，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Shou, courtesy name Changshou, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shou, whose courtesy name was Changshou, came from Luoyang in Henan commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖敦，魏侍中、邵陵王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dun was Palace Attendant under Wei and Prince of Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dun had served as Palace Attendant under Wei and held the title Prince of Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 父寶，周涼州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Bao was Inspector of Liangzhou under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bao had served as Inspector of Liangzhou under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 壽少孤，性仁孝，九歲喪父，哀毀骨立，宗族鄉黨咸異之。

translations.literal: Shou lost his father while young; his nature was benevolent and filial; at nine he lost his father and was so grief-stricken that only skin and bone remained — clan and village neighbors all marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was orphaned young. Benevolent and filial by nature, he lost his father at nine and grieved until he was skin and bone; kin and neighbors alike marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: In serving his mother he was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for filial devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 及長，方直，頗涉文史。

translations.literal: When he grew up he was upright and square, and had considerable exposure to literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he was upright and principled and had considerable training in literature and history.

sentences.zh: 周武成初，封隆城縣侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng under Zhou he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Longcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Wucheng's reign he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Longcheng County.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，封儀隴縣侯，授儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yilong County and granted Attendant Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Baoding he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yilong County and granted the rank of Attendant Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，議伐陳，以壽有思理，使於淮浦監修船艦，以強濟見稱。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang under Sui, when an attack on Chen was under discussion, because Shou had thoughtful reasoning he was sent to the Huai River shore to supervise the building of ships, and was praised for strength and efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaihuang era, when the court debated an attack on Chen, Shou was sent to the Huai River shore to supervise shipbuilding because of his sound judgment, and was praised for his vigor and efficiency.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 文帝嘗出苑觀射，文武並從。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen once went out to the park to watch archery; civil and military officials all followed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once went out to the park to watch archery, with civil and military officials in attendance.

sentences.zh: 開府蕭摩訶妻患且死，奏請遣子向江南收其家產，御史見而不言。

translations.literal: The wife of the Office Opener Xiao Mohe was ill and near death; he memorialized requesting that his son be sent south to the Jiang region to recover their family property, and the censor saw it and said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Grand Master Opening the Office Xiao Mohe was gravely ill and near death. He memorialized asking that his son be sent south to the Jiang region to recover their family property, and the attending censor saw it and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 壽奏劾之曰：「御史之官，義存糾察，直繩莫舉，憲典誰寄？

translations.literal: Shou submitted an impeachment, saying, "The office of censor exists to preserve correction and investigation; if the straight cord is not applied, to whom is the authority of the statutes entrusted?
translations.idiomatic: Shou submitted an impeachment memorial: "The censor's office exists to preserve correction and investigation. If the straight cord of justice is not applied, to whom can the authority of the statutes be entrusted?

sentences.zh: 今月五日，鑾輿徙蹕，親臨射苑，開府儀同三司蕭摩訶幸廁朝行，預觀盛禮，奏稱請遣子世略暫往江南重收家產。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of this month the imperial carriage moved with halting of traffic and personally attended the archery park; the Office Opener and Attendant Equal to the Three Dukes Xiao Mohe had the privilege of attending at court ranks, took part in viewing the grand ceremony, and memorialized requesting that his son Shilue be temporarily sent south to the Jiang region to recover the family property again.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of this month the imperial carriage moved with full halting of traffic to attend the archery park in person. Grand Master Opening the Office and Attendant Equal to the Three Dukes Xiao Mohe, privileged to attend at court ranks, took part in the grand ceremony and memorialized asking that his son Shilue be temporarily sent south to the Jiang region to recover the family property.

sentences.zh: 妻安遇患，彌留有日，安若長逝，世略不合此行。

translations.literal: His wife An is afflicted with illness and has but days remaining; if An should pass away, Shilue ought not to make this journey.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady An is gravely ill and has but days remaining. If she should pass away, Shilue ought not to undertake such a journey.

sentences.zh: 竊以人倫之義，伉儷為重，資愛之道，烏烏弗虧。

translations.literal: I venture to hold that in the principles of human relations, the bond of husband and wife is paramount; in the way of nourishing love, the devotion of the crow is not diminished.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that among the bonds of human relations, the marriage tie is paramount, and that the way of nourishing love — like the crow's devotion to its parents — must not be diminished.

sentences.zh: 摩訶遠念資財，近忘匹好，一言才發，名教頓盡，而兼殿內侍御史臣韓征之等親所聞見，竟不彈糾。

translations.literal: Mohe, thinking far of property and forgetting near the bond of spouse, with one word just spoken utterly destroyed moral teaching in an instant; yet the Concurrent Palace Attendant Censor Han Zhengzhi and others personally heard and saw it and in the end did not impeach and censure.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe, brooding over distant property while forgetting the bond at his side, with a single utterance destroyed the moral order in an instant. Yet Concurrent Palace Attendant Censor Han Zhengzhi and others heard and saw it with their own ears and eyes and still did not impeach him.

sentences.zh: 若知非不舉，情涉阿縱；

translations.literal: If they knew it was wrong and did not report it, their feeling involved partiality and indulgence;
translations.idiomatic: If they knew it was wrong and did not report it, they were guilty of partiality and indulgence;

sentences.zh: 如不以為非，豈關理識？

translations.literal: if they did not consider it wrong, what has that to do with reason and discernment?
translations.idiomatic: if they did not consider it wrong, what then becomes of their reason and discernment?

sentences.zh: 儀同三司、太子左庶子、檢校書侍御史臣劉行本虧失憲體，何所逃愆？

translations.literal: Attendant Equal to the Three Dukes, Left Assistant to the Crown Prince, and Supervisory Secretary Attendant Censor Liu Xingben has failed the integrity of the censorate — from what fault can he escape?
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Equal to the Three Dukes, Left Assistant to the Crown Prince, and Supervisory Secretary Attendant Censor Liu Xingben has failed the integrity of the censorate — what fault can he escape?

sentences.zh: 臣謬膺朝寄，忝居左轄，無容寢默，謹以狀聞。」

translations.literal: Your subject has wrongly received the court's charge and humbly occupies the left reins; I cannot remain silent and respectfully report this by memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has wrongly received the court's charge and humbly holds the left vice-directorship; I cannot remain silent and respectfully report this matter."

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 後授太常少卿，出為基州刺史，有公廉稱。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Junior Minister of Ceremonies, sent out as Inspector of Jizhou, and had a reputation for public integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Junior Minister of Ceremonies and sent out as Inspector of Jizhou, where he won a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 入為太府少卿，進位開府。

translations.literal: He entered service as Junior Minister of the Imperial Storehouse and was advanced to Office Opener.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Junior Minister of the Imperial Storehouse and was promoted to Grand Master Opening the Office.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，漢王諒反，左僕射楊素為行軍元帥，壽為長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, the Prince of Han, Liang, rebelled; Left Vice Director Yang Su was campaigning commander-in-chief and Shou was chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Prince Liang of Han rebelled. Left Vice Director Yang Su served as campaigning commander-in-chief, with Shou as his chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 事平，以功授大將軍。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, for merit he was granted General.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was suppressed, he was granted the rank of General for his merit.

sentences.zh: 遷太府卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Imperial Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of the Imperial Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 大業四年，拜內史令，從帝西討吐谷渾，壽率眾屯金山，東西連營三百餘里以圍渾主。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daye he was appointed Director of the Inner Scribe's Office; he followed the Emperor on the western campaign against Tuyuhun, and Shou led troops to encamp at Jinshan, linking camps east and west for more than three hundred li to surround the Tuyuhun ruler.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daye he was made Director of the Inner Scribe's Office and accompanied the emperor on the western expedition against Tuyuhun. Shou led his forces to Jinshan and drew up a continuous line of camps more than three hundred li long, east to west, to hem in the Tuyuhun ruler.

sentences.zh: 還拜右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Right Grand Master with Golden Seal.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Right Grand Master with Golden Seal.

sentences.zh: 七年，兼左翊衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was additionally made General of the Left Wing Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was additionally made General of the Left Wing Guard.

sentences.zh: 從征遼東，在道卒。

translations.literal: He followed the expedition to Liaodong and died on the march.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Liaodong campaign and died on the road.

sentences.zh: 帝哭之甚慟，贈尚書右僕射、光祿大夫，諡曰景。

translations.literal: The Emperor wept for him with deep grief, posthumously granted him Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and Grand Master with Golden Seal, and gave him the posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him with deep grief, posthumously appointing him Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and Grand Master with Golden Seal, with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 子敏，頗有才辯，而輕險多詐。

translations.literal: His son Min was rather talented in eloquence and debate, but frivolous, rash, and full of deceit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Min was clever and articulate, but reckless, unscrupulous, and given to deceit.

sentences.zh: 壽卒，帝追思之，擢敏守內史舍人。

translations.literal: When Shou died, the Emperor recalled him with longing and promoted Min to serve as Secretary in the Inner Scribe's Office.
translations.idiomatic: After Shou's death the emperor, thinking fondly of him, promoted Min to secretary in the Inner Scribe's Office.

sentences.zh: 交通博徒，數泄省中語。

translations.literal: He associated with gamblers and repeatedly leaked matters discussed within the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He consorted with gamblers and repeatedly leaked confidential business from the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 化及之反，敏創其謀，偽授內史侍郎，為沈光所殺。

translations.literal: When Huaji rebelled, Min was the originator of the plot; he was falsely appointed Vice Director of the Inner Scribe's Office and was killed by Shen Guang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji rebelled, Min was the chief architect of the conspiracy; he was given the false title of Vice Director of the Inner Scribe's Office and was killed by Shen Guang.

translations.literal: 【Discussion】
translations.idiomatic: Discussion

sentences.zh: 論曰：二趙明習故事，當世咸推，及居端右，無聞殊績。

translations.literal: The commentary says: The two Zhao were clear and practiced in precedent, and all their age praised them; yet when they stood at the head of government, no outstanding achievements were heard of.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: The two Zhao were thoroughly versed in court precedent and widely admired in their day, yet once they reached the highest offices, no exceptional achievements were recorded.

sentences.zh: 故知人之分器，各有量限，大小雲異，不可相逾。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that men's allotted vessels each have their measure and limit; great and small differ like clouds, and one cannot cross beyond them.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that each man's capacity has its measure and limit; talents differ in scale as clouds differ in height, and one cannot be forced beyond what he is fit for.

sentences.zh: 晉蜀二王，帝之愛子，擅以權寵，莫拘憲法。

translations.literal: The two princes of Jin and Shu, the Emperor's beloved sons, monopolized power and favor and were bound by no law or statute.
translations.idiomatic: The princes of Jin and Shu, the emperor's beloved sons, wielded unchecked power and privilege and answered to no law.

sentences.zh: 王韶、元岩任當彼相，並見嚴憚，莫敢為非，謇諤之風有足稱矣。

translations.literal: Wang Shao and Yuan Yan filled the role of ministers to them; both were regarded with stern awe, and none dared do wrong—their forthright remonstrating spirit is well worth praise.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao and Yuan Yan served them in the capacity of chief ministers; both inspired such respect that no one dared misconduct himself—their tradition of bold remonstrance is indeed praiseworthy.

sentences.zh: 宇文弼宇量宏遠，聲望攸歸，斯言不密，以致傾殞，惜矣！

translations.literal: Yuwen Bi's breadth of mind was vast and far-reaching, and public esteem turned to him; because this speech was not kept secret, he came to ruin and death—how regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Bi's vision was broad and his reputation commanding; because a private remark was not kept secret, he was destroyed—a grievous loss!

sentences.zh: 伊婁謙志識弘深，不念舊惡，請赦高遵之罪，有君子風焉。

translations.literal: Yi Louqian's will and insight were broad and deep; he did not bear old enmity in mind and asked to pardon Gao Zun's crime—there was the manner of a gentleman in this.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Louqian was magnanimous in purpose and judgment; forgetting old injuries, he pleaded for Gao Zun's pardon—truly the conduct of a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 李圓通、郭榮、龐晃等或陳力經綸之際，或自結龍潛之始，其所以高位厚秩，隆恩殊寵，豈徒然哉！

translations.literal: Li Yuantong, Guo Rong, Pang Huang, and the like either displayed their strength in the time of ordering the realm, or bound themselves from the beginning when the dragon lay hidden; that they received high rank and rich stipends, lofty favor and special grace—was it for nothing!
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuantong, Guo Rong, Pang Huang, and others either proved their worth while the empire was being ordered, or attached themselves when Yang Jian was still in obscurity; their high offices, rich rewards, and extraordinary favor were not given without cause.

sentences.zh: 李安雖則滅親，而於義亦已疏矣。

translations.literal: Though Li An destroyed his kin, in righteousness he was already estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Though Li An sacrificed kinship for duty, even in moral terms the bond had already been severed.

sentences.zh: 楊尚希譽望隆重，張煚、蘇孝慈威稱貞幹，並擢自開皇之初，蓋當時之選也。

translations.literal: Yang Shangxi's reputation and standing were weighty; Zhang Jiong and Su Xiaoci were famed in authority as upright and capable—all were raised at the beginning of Kaihuang; they were the choice men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shangxi enjoyed great prestige; Zhang Jiong and Su Xiaoci were renowned for upright and capable administration—all were promoted at the start of the Kaihuang era and were among the finest appointments of their time.

sentences.zh: 元壽之彈行本，有意存夫名教。

translations.literal: Yuan Shou's impeachment of Xing Ben was intended to preserve the teaching of names and morals.
translations.idiomatic: In impeaching Xing Ben, Yuan Shou sought to uphold the moral order.

sentences.zh: 然其計功稱伐，蓋不足雲，端揆之贈，則為優矣。

translations.literal: Yet in reckoning merit and proclaiming achievements, he can scarcely be mentioned; the gift of the highest ministerial rank, however, was generous indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet measured by actual achievement, he hardly merits mention; the posthumous grant of a chief-minister's rank, on the other hand, was remarkably generous.
